units.rightText: Speak unto Aaron, and say unto him, When thou lightest the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the candlestick.

units.leftText: And Aaron did so; he set up the lamps facing toward the front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And Aaron did so; he lighted the lamps thereof so as to give light in front of the candlestick, as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: This is how the lampstand was constructed: it was made of hammered gold from its base to its blossoms, fashioned according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses. Cleansing the Levites
units.rightText: And this was the work of the candlestick, beaten work of gold; unto the base thereof, and unto the flowers thereof, it was beaten work: according unto the pattern which Jehovah had showed Moses, so he made the candlestick.

units.leftText: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.
units.rightText: Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them.

units.leftText: This is what you must do to cleanse them: Sprinkle them with the water of purification. Have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so purify themselves.
units.rightText: And thus shalt thou do unto them, to cleanse them: sprinkle the water of expiation upon them, and let them cause a razor to pass over all their flesh, and let them wash their clothes, and cleanse themselves.

units.leftText: Then have them take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.
units.rightText: Then let them take a young bullock, and its meal-offering, fine flour mingled with oil; and another young bullock shalt thou take for a sin-offering.

units.leftText: Bring the Levites before the Tent of Meeting and assemble the whole congregation of Israel.
units.rightText: And thou shalt present the Levites before the tent of meeting: and thou shalt assemble the whole congregation of the children of Israel:

units.leftText: You are to present the Levites before the LORD and have the Israelites lay their hands upon them.
units.rightText: and thou shalt present the Levites before Jehovah. And the children of Israel shall lay their hands upon the Levites:

units.leftText: Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the sons of Israel, so that they may perform the service of the LORD.
units.rightText: and Aaron shall offer the Levites before Jehovah for a wave-offering, on the behalf of the children of Israel, that it may be theirs to do the service of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and offer to the LORD one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, to make atonement for the Levites.
units.rightText: And the Levites shall lay their hands upon the heads of the bullocks: and offer thou the one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering, unto Jehovah, to make atonement for the Levites.

units.leftText: You are to have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons and then present them before the LORD as a wave offering.
units.rightText: And thou shalt set the Levites before Aaron, and before his sons, and offer them for a wave-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: In this way you shall separate the Levites from the rest of the Israelites, and the Levites will belong to Me.
units.rightText: Thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the children of Israel; and the Levites shall be mine.

units.leftText: After you have cleansed them and presented them as a wave offering, they may come to serve at the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And after that shall the Levites go in to do the service of the tent of meeting: and thou shalt cleanse them, and offer them for a wave-offering.

units.leftText: For the Levites have been wholly given to Me from among the sons of Israel. I have taken them for Myself in place of all who come first from the womb, the firstborn of all the sons of Israel.
units.rightText: For they are wholly given unto me from among the children of Israel; instead of all that openeth the womb, even the first-born of all the children of Israel, have I taken them unto me.

units.leftText: For every firstborn male in Israel is Mine, both man and beast. I set them apart for Myself on the day I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: For all the first-born among the children of Israel are mine, both man and beast: on the day that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt I sanctified them for myself.

units.leftText: But I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the sons of Israel.
units.rightText: And I have taken the Levites instead of all the first-born among the children of Israel.

units.leftText: And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service for the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting and to make atonement on their behalf, so that no plague will come against the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.”
units.rightText: And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the tent of meeting, and to make atonement for the children of Israel; that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come nigh unto the sanctuary.

units.leftText: So Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of Israel did with the Levites everything that the LORD had commanded Moses they should do.
units.rightText: Thus did Moses, and Aaron, and all the congregation of the children of Israel, unto the Levites: according unto all that Jehovah commanded Moses touching the Levites, so did the children of Israel unto them.

units.leftText: The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes, and Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD. Aaron also made atonement for them to cleanse them.
units.rightText: And the Levites purified themselves from sin, and they washed their clothes: and Aaron offered them for a wave-offering before Jehovah; and Aaron made atonement for them to cleanse them.

units.leftText: After that, the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting in the presence of Aaron and his sons. Thus they did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses. Retirement for Levites
units.rightText: And after that went the Levites in to do their service in the tent of meeting before Aaron, and before his sons: as Jehovah had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so did they unto them.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “This applies to the Levites: Men twenty-five years of age or older shall enter to perform the service in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: This is that which belongeth unto the Levites: from twenty and five years old and upward they shall go in to wait upon the service in the work of the tent of meeting:

units.leftText: But at the age of fifty, they must retire from performing the work and no longer serve.
units.rightText: and from the age of fifty years they shall cease waiting upon the work, and shall serve no more,

units.leftText: After that, they may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work. This is how you are to assign responsibilities to the Levites.”
units.rightText: but shall minister with their brethren in the tent of meeting, to keep the charge, and shall do no service. Thus shalt thou do unto the Levites touching their charges.

units.leftText: In the first month of the second year after Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai:
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they were come out of the land of Egypt, saying,

units.leftText: “The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time.
units.rightText: Moreover let the children of Israel keep the passover in its appointed season.

units.leftText: You are to observe it at the appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, in accordance with its statutes and ordinances.”
units.rightText: In the fourteenth day of this month, at even, ye shall keep it in its appointed season: according to all the statutes of it, and according to all the ordinances thereof, shall ye keep it.
leftNotes: 9:3 Hebrew between the two evenings of the fourteenth; also in verses 5 and 11

units.leftText: So Moses told the Israelites to observe the Passover,
units.rightText: And Moses spake unto the children of Israel, that they should keep the passover.

units.leftText: and they did so in the Wilderness of Sinai, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And they kept the passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at even, in the wilderness of Sinai: according to all that Jehovah commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel.

units.leftText: But there were some men who were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day. And they came before Moses and Aaron that same day
units.rightText: And there were certain men, who were unclean by reason of the dead body of a man, so that they could not keep the passover on that day: and they came before Moses and before Aaron on that day:

units.leftText: and said to Moses, “We are unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?”
units.rightText: and those men said unto him, We are unclean by reason of the dead body of a man: wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer the oblation of Jehovah in its appointed season among the children of Israel?

units.leftText: “Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you,” Moses replied.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto them, Stay ye, that I may hear what Jehovah will command concerning you.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell the Israelites: ‘When any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If any man of you or of your generations shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be on a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They are to eat the lamb, together with unleavened bread and bitter herbs;
units.rightText: In the second month on the fourteenth day at even they shall keep it; they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs:

units.leftText: they may not leave any of it until morning or break any of its bones. They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes.
units.rightText: they shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break a bone thereof: according to all the statute of the passover they shall keep it.

units.leftText: But if a man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey still fails to observe the Passover, he must be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD’s offering at its appointed time. That man will bear the consequences of his sin.
units.rightText: But the man that is clean, and is not on a journey, and forbeareth to keep the passover, that soul shall be cut off from his people; because he offered not the oblation of Jehovah in its appointed season, that man shall bear his sin.

units.leftText: If a foreigner dwelling among you wants to observe the Passover to the LORD, he is to do so according to the Passover statute and its ordinances. You are to apply the same statute to both the foreigner and the native of the land.’” The Cloud above the Tabernacle (Exodus 40:34–38|EXO 40:34-38*)
units.rightText: And if a stranger shall sojourn among you, and will keep the passover unto Jehovah; according to the statute of the passover, and according to the ordinance thereof, so shall he do: ye shall have one statute, both for the sojourner, and for him that is born in the land.

units.leftText: On the day that the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony, was set up, the cloud covered it and appeared like fire above the tabernacle from evening until morning.
units.rightText: And on the day that the tabernacle was reared up the cloud covered the tabernacle, even the tent of the testimony: and at even it was upon the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire, until morning.

units.leftText: It remained that way continually; the cloud would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire.
units.rightText: So it was alway: the cloud covered it, and the appearance of fire by night.
leftNotes: 9:16 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew does not include by day

units.leftText: Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the Tent, the Israelites would set out, and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.
units.rightText: And whenever the cloud was taken up from over the Tent, then after that the children of Israel journeyed: and in the place where the cloud abode, there the children of Israel encamped.

units.leftText: At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they camped. As long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, they remained encamped.
units.rightText: At the commandment of Jehovah the children of Israel journeyed, and at the commandment of Jehovah they encamped: as long as the cloud abode upon the tabernacle they remained encamped.

units.leftText: Even when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the LORD’s charge and did not set out.
units.rightText: And when the cloud tarried upon the tabernacle many days, then the children of Israel kept the charge of Jehovah, and journeyed not.

units.leftText: Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle for only a few days, and they would camp at the LORD’s command and set out at the LORD’s command.
units.rightText: And sometimes the cloud was a few days upon the tabernacle; then according to the commandment of Jehovah they remained encamped, and according to the commandment of Jehovah they journeyed.

units.leftText: Sometimes the cloud remained only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they would set out. Whether it was by day or by night, when the cloud was taken up, they would set out.
units.rightText: And sometimes the cloud was from evening until morning; and when the cloud was taken up in the morning, they journeyed: or if it continued by day and by night, when the cloud was taken up, they journeyed.

units.leftText: Whether the cloud lingered for two days, a month, or longer, the Israelites camped and did not set out as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle; but when it was lifted, they would set out.
units.rightText: Whether it were two days, or a month, or a year, that the cloud tarried upon the tabernacle, abiding thereon, the children of Israel remained encamped, and journeyed not; but when it was taken up, they journeyed.

units.leftText: They camped at the LORD’s command, and they set out at the LORD’s command; they carried out the LORD’s charge according to His command through Moses.
units.rightText: At the commandment of Jehovah they encamped, and at the commandment of Jehovah they journeyed: they kept the charge of Jehovah, at the commandment of Jehovah by Moses.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Make two trumpets of hammered silver to be used for calling the congregation and for having the camps set out.
units.rightText: Make thee two trumpets of silver; of beaten work shalt thou make them: and thou shalt use them for the calling of the congregation, and for the journeying of the camps.

units.leftText: When both are sounded, the whole congregation is to assemble before you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And when they shall blow them, all the congregation shall gather themselves unto thee at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: But if only one is sounded, then the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, are to gather before you.
units.rightText: And if they blow but one, then the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather themselves unto thee.

units.leftText: When you sound short blasts, the camps that lie on the east side are to set out.
units.rightText: And when ye blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the east side shall take their journey.

units.leftText: When you sound the short blasts a second time, the camps that lie on the south side are to set out. The blasts are to signal them to set out.
units.rightText: And when ye blow an alarm the second time, the camps that lie on the south side shall take their journey: they shall blow an alarm for their journeys.

units.leftText: To convene the assembly, you are to sound long blasts, not short ones.
units.rightText: But when the assembly is to be gathered together, ye shall blow, but ye shall not sound an alarm.

units.leftText: The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to sound the trumpets. This shall be a permanent statute for you and the generations to come.
units.rightText: And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; and they shall be to you for a statute for ever throughout your generations.

units.leftText: When you enter into battle in your land against an adversary who attacks you, sound short blasts on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.
units.rightText: And when ye go to war in your land against the adversary that oppresseth you, then ye shall sound an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before Jehovah your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies.

units.leftText: And on your joyous occasions, your appointed feasts, and the beginning of each month, you are to blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings to serve as a reminder for you before your God. I am the LORD your God.” From Sinai to Paran
units.rightText: Also in the day of your gladness, and in your set feasts, and in the beginnings of your months, ye shall blow the trumpets over your burnt-offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings; and they shall be to you for a memorial before your God: I am Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony,
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, that the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony.

units.leftText: and the Israelites set out from the Wilderness of Sinai, traveling from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel set forward according to their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran.

units.leftText: They set out this first time according to the LORD’s command through Moses.
units.rightText: And they first took their journey according to the commandment of Jehovah by Moses.

units.leftText: First, the divisions of the camp of Judah set out under their standard, with Nahshon son of Amminadab in command.
units.rightText: And in the first place the standard of the camp of the children of Judah set forward according to their hosts: and over his host was Nahshon the son of Amminadab.

units.leftText: Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar,
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Issachar was Nethanel the son of Zuar.

units.leftText: and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Zebulun was Eliab the son of Helon.

units.leftText: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites set out, transporting it.
units.rightText: And the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who bare the tabernacle, set forward.

units.leftText: Then the divisions of the camp of Reuben set out under their standard, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command.
units.rightText: And the standard of the camp of Reuben set forward according to their hosts: and over his host was Elizur the son of Shedeur.

units.leftText: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon,
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Simeon was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.

units.leftText: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Gad was Eliasaph the son of Deuel.

units.leftText: Then the Kohathites set out, transporting the holy objects; the tabernacle was to be set up before their arrival.
units.rightText: And the Kohathites set forward, bearing the sanctuary: and the others did set up the tabernacle against their coming.

units.leftText: Next, the divisions of the camp of Ephraim set out under their standard, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command.
units.rightText: And the standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim set forward according to their hosts: and over his host was Elishama the son of Ammihud.

units.leftText: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh,
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Manasseh was Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.

units.leftText: and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Benjamin was Abidan the son of Gideoni.

units.leftText: Finally, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out under their standard, serving as the rear guard for all units, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command.
units.rightText: And the standard of the camp of the children of Dan, which was the rearward of all the camps, set forward according to their hosts: and over his host was Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.

units.leftText: Pagiel son of Ocran was over the division of the tribe of Asher,
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Asher was Pagiel the son of Ochran.

units.leftText: and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
units.rightText: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Naphtali was Ahira the son of Enan.

units.leftText: This was the order of march for the Israelite divisions as they set out.
units.rightText: Thus were the journeyings of the children of Israel according to their hosts; and they set forward.

units.leftText: Then Moses said to Hobab, the son of Moses’ father-in-law Reuel the Midianite, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said: ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Hobab, the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, We are journeying unto the place of which Jehovah said, I will give it you: come thou with us, and we will do thee good; for Jehovah hath spoken good concerning Israel.
leftNotes: 10:29 Reuel was also called Jethro; see Exodus 3:1|EXO 3:1*.

units.leftText: “I will not go,” Hobab replied. “Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, I will not go; but I will depart to mine own land, and to my kindred.

units.leftText: “Please do not leave us,” Moses said, “since you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can serve as our eyes.
units.rightText: And he said, Leave us not, I pray thee; forasmuch as thou knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness, and thou shalt be to us instead of eyes.

units.leftText: If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us.”
units.rightText: And it shall be, if thou go with us, yea, it shall be, that what good soever Jehovah shall do unto us, the same will we do unto thee.

units.leftText: So they set out on a three-day journey from the mountain of the LORD, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD traveling ahead of them for those three days to seek a resting place for them.
units.rightText: And they set forward from the mount of Jehovah three days’ journey; and the ark of the covenant of Jehovah went before them three days’ journey, to seek out a resting-place for them.

units.leftText: And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
units.rightText: And the cloud of Jehovah was over them by day, when they set forward from the camp.

units.leftText: Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said, Rise up, O Jehovah, and let thine enemies be scattered; and let them that hate thee flee before thee.

units.leftText: And when it came to rest, he would say: “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel.”
units.rightText: And when it rested, he said, Return, O Jehovah, unto the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.

units.leftText: Soon the people began to complain about their hardship in the hearing of the LORD, and when He heard them, His anger was kindled, and fire from the LORD blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
units.rightText: And the people were as murmurers, speaking evil in the ears of Jehovah: and when Jehovah heard it, his anger was kindled; and the fire of Jehovah burnt among them, and devoured in the uttermost part of the camp.

units.leftText: And the people cried out to Moses, and he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
units.rightText: And the people cried unto Moses; and Moses prayed unto Jehovah, and the fire abated.

units.leftText: So that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
units.rightText: And the name of that place was called Taberah, because the fire of Jehovah burnt among them.
leftNotes: 11:3 Taberah means burning.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the rabble among them had a strong craving for other food, and again the Israelites wept and said, “Who will feed us meat?
units.rightText: And the mixed multitude that was among them lusted exceedingly: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?

units.leftText: We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt, along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
units.rightText: We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt for nought; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic:

units.leftText: But now our appetite is gone; there is nothing to see but this manna!”
units.rightText: but now our soul is dried away; there is nothing at all save this manna to look upon.

units.leftText: Now the manna resembled coriander seed, and its appearance was like that of gum resin.
units.rightText: And the manna was like coriander seed, and the appearance thereof as the appearance of bdellium.

units.leftText: The people walked around and gathered it, ground it on a handmill or crushed it in a mortar, then boiled it in a cooking pot or shaped it into cakes. It tasted like pastry baked with fine oil.
units.rightText: The people went about, and gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it: and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil.

units.leftText: When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna would fall with it. The Complaint of Moses
units.rightText: And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell upon it.

units.leftText: Then Moses heard the people of family after family weeping at the entrances to their tents, and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly, and Moses was also displeased.
units.rightText: And Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, every man at the door of his tent: and the anger of Jehovah was kindled greatly; and Moses was displeased.

units.leftText: So Moses asked the LORD, “Why have You brought this trouble on Your servant? Why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You have laid upon me the burden of all these people?
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Jehovah, Wherefore hast thou dealt ill with thy servant? and wherefore have I not found favor in thy sight, that thou layest the burden of all this people upon me?

units.leftText: Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth, so that You should tell me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries an infant,’ to the land that You swore to give their fathers?
units.rightText: Have I conceived all this people? have I brought them forth, that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing-father carrieth the sucking child, unto the land which thou swarest unto their fathers?

units.leftText: Where can I get meat for all these people? For they keep crying out to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’
units.rightText: Whence should I have flesh to give unto all this people? for they weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.

units.leftText: I cannot carry all these people by myself; it is too burdensome for me.
units.rightText: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.

units.leftText: If this is how You are going to treat me, please kill me right now — if I have found favor in Your eyes — and let me not see my own wretchedness.” Seventy Elders Anointed
units.rightText: And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favor in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them unto the tent of meeting, that they may stand there with thee.

units.leftText: And I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them. They will help you bear the burden of the people, so that you do not have to bear it by yourself.
units.rightText: And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the Spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.

units.leftText: And say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, because you have cried out in the hearing of the LORD, saying: ‘Who will feed us meat? For we were better off in Egypt!’ Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
units.rightText: And say thou unto the people, Sanctify yourselves against to-morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; for ye have wept in the ears of Jehovah, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for it was well with us in Egypt: therefore Jehovah will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.

units.leftText: You will eat it not for one or two days, nor for five or ten or twenty days,
units.rightText: Ye shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days,

units.leftText: but for a whole month— until it comes out of your nostrils and makes you nauseous— because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried out before Him, saying, ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’”
units.rightText: but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils, and it be loathsome unto you; because that ye have rejected Jehovah who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we forth out of Egypt?

units.leftText: But Moses replied, “Here I am among 600,000 men on foot, yet You say, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a month.’
units.rightText: And Moses said, The people, among whom I am, are six hundred thousand footmen; and thou hast said, I will give them flesh, that they may eat a whole month.

units.leftText: If all our flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would they have enough? Or if all the fish in the sea were caught for them, would they have enough?”
units.rightText: Shall flocks and herds be slain for them, to suffice them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to suffice them?

units.leftText: The LORD answered Moses, “Is the LORD’s arm too short? Now you will see whether or not My word will come to pass.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Is Jehovah’s hand waxed short? now shalt thou see whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not.

units.leftText: So Moses went out and relayed to the people the words of the LORD, and he gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.
units.rightText: And Moses went out, and told the people the words of Jehovah: and he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the Tent.

units.leftText: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed that Spirit on the seventy elders. As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied — but they never did so again.
units.rightText: And Jehovah came down in the cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the Spirit that was upon him, and put it upon the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, but they did so no more.

units.leftText: Two men, however, had remained in the camp — one named Eldad and the other Medad — and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
units.rightText: But there remained two men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but had not gone out unto the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp.

units.leftText: A young man ran and reported to Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
units.rightText: And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.

units.leftText: Joshua son of Nun, the attendant to Moses since youth, spoke up and said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”
units.rightText: And Joshua the son of Nun, the minister of Moses, one of his chosen men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.

units.leftText: But Moses replied, “Are you jealous on my account? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto him, Art thou jealous for my sake? would that all Jehovah’s people were prophets, that Jehovah would put his Spirit upon them!

units.leftText: Then Moses returned to the camp, along with the elders of Israel. The Quail and the Plague
units.rightText: And Moses gat him into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

units.leftText: Now a wind sent by the LORD came up, drove in quail from the sea, and brought them near the camp, about two cubits above the surface of the ground, for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.
units.rightText: And there went forth a wind from Jehovah, and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and a day’s journey on the other side, round about the camp, and about two cubits above the face of the earth.
leftNotes: 11:31 Or up to two cubits deep; that is, approximately 3 feet or 91.4 centimeters

units.leftText: All that day and night, and all the next day, the people stayed up gathering the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.
units.rightText: And the people rose up all that day, and all the night, and all the next day, and gathered the quails: he that gathered least gathered ten homers: and they spread them all abroad for themselves round about the camp.
leftNotes: 11:32 10 homers is approximately 62.4 bushels or 2,200 liters.

units.leftText: But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck them with a severe plague.
units.rightText: While the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the anger of Jehovah was kindled against the people, and Jehovah smote the people with a very great plague.

units.leftText: So they called that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
units.rightText: And the name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people that lusted.
leftNotes: 11:34 Kibroth-hattaavah means graves of craving.

units.leftText: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.
units.rightText: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people journeyed unto Hazeroth; and they abode at Hazeroth.

units.leftText: Then Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had taken a Cushite wife.
units.rightText: And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married; for he had married a Cushite woman.

units.leftText: “Does the LORD speak only through Moses?” they said. “Does He not also speak through us?” And the LORD heard this.
units.rightText: And they said, Hath Jehovah indeed spoken only with Moses? hath he not spoken also with us? And Jehovah heard it.

units.leftText: Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than any man on the face of the earth.
units.rightText: Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men that were upon the face of the earth.

units.leftText: And suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “You three, come out to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three went out,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake suddenly unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, Come out ye three unto the tent of meeting. And they three came out.

units.leftText: and the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance to the Tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam. When both of them had stepped forward,
units.rightText: And Jehovah came down in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the door of the Tent, and called Aaron and Miriam; and they both came forth.

units.leftText: He said, “Hear now My words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, will reveal Myself to him in a vision; I will speak to him in a dream.
units.rightText: And he said, Hear now my words: if there be a prophet among you, I Jehovah will make myself known unto him in a vision, I will speak with him in a dream.

units.leftText: But this is not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
units.rightText: My servant Moses is not so; he is faithful in all my house:
leftNotes: 12:7 Cited in Hebrews 3:5|HEB 3:5*

units.leftText: I speak with him face to face, clearly and not in riddles; he sees the form of the LORD.
units.rightText: with him will I speak mouth to mouth, even manifestly, and not in dark speeches; and the form of Jehovah shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?

units.leftText: So the anger of the LORD burned against them, and He departed.
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against them; and he departed.

units.leftText: As the cloud lifted from above the Tent, suddenly Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her, saw that she was leprous,
units.rightText: And the cloud removed from over the Tent; and, behold, Miriam was leprous, as white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.
leftNotes: 12:10 The Hebrew word traditionally translated as leprous was used for various skin diseases; see Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: and said to Moses, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.
units.rightText: And Aaron said unto Moses, Oh, my lord, lay not, I pray thee, sin upon us, for that we have done foolishly, and for that we have sinned.

units.leftText: Please do not let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb.”
units.rightText: Let her not, I pray, be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he cometh out of his mother’s womb.

units.leftText: So Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!”
units.rightText: And Moses cried unto Jehovah, saying, Heal her, O God, I beseech thee.

units.leftText: But the LORD answered Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, would she not have been in disgrace for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days; after that she may be brought back in.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut up without the camp seven days, and after that she shall be brought in again.

units.leftText: So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought in again.
units.rightText: And Miriam was shut up without the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.

units.leftText: After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.
units.rightText: And afterward the people journeyed from Hazeroth, and encamped in the wilderness of Paran.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Send out for yourself men to spy out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each of their fathers’ tribes send one man who is a leader among them.”
units.rightText: Send thou men, that they may spy out the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel: of every tribe of their fathers shall ye send a man, every one a prince among them.

units.leftText: So at the command of the LORD, Moses sent them out from the Wilderness of Paran. All the men were leaders of the Israelites,
units.rightText: And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran according to the commandment of Jehovah: all of them men who were heads of the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 13:3 Literally according to the mouth

units.leftText: and these were their names: From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
units.rightText: And these were their names: Of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Manasseh (a tribe of Joseph), Gaddi son of Susi;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Joseph, namely, of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.

units.leftText: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.

units.leftText: and from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
units.rightText: Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.

units.leftText: These were the names of the men Moses sent to spy out the land; and Moses gave to Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
units.rightText: These are the names of the men that Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses called Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua.

units.leftText: When Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, he told them, “Go up through the Negev and into the hill country.
units.rightText: And Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, and said unto them, Get you up this way by the South, and go up into the hill-country:

units.leftText: See what the land is like and whether its people are strong or weak, few or many.
units.rightText: and see the land, what it is; and the people that dwell therein, whether they are strong or weak, whether they are few or many;

units.leftText: Is the land where they live good or bad? Are the cities where they dwell open camps or fortifications?
units.rightText: and what the land is that they dwell in, whether it is good or bad; and what cities they are that they dwell in, whether in camps, or in strongholds;

units.leftText: Is the soil fertile or unproductive? Are there trees in it or not? Be courageous and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” (It was the season for the first ripe grapes.)
units.rightText: and what the land is, whether it is fat or lean, whether there is wood therein, or not. And be ye of good courage, and bring of the fruit of the land. Now the time was the time of the first-ripe grapes.

units.leftText: So they went up and spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.
units.rightText: So they went up, and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin unto Rehob, to the entrance of Hamath.

units.leftText: They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, dwelled. It had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
units.rightText: And they went up by the South, and came unto Hebron; and Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, were there. (Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)

units.leftText: When they came to the Valley of Eshcol, they cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which they carried on a pole between two men. They also took some pomegranates and figs.
units.rightText: And they came unto the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it upon a staff between two; they brought also of the pomegranates, and of the figs.
leftNotes: 13:23 Eshcol means cluster; also in verse 24.

units.leftText: Because of the cluster of grapes the Israelites cut there, that place was called the Valley of Eshcol. The Reports of the Spies
units.rightText: That place was called the valley of Eshcol, because of the cluster which the children of Israel cut down from thence.

units.leftText: After forty days the men returned from spying out the land,
units.rightText: And they returned from spying out the land at the end of forty days.

units.leftText: and they went back to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of Israel in the Wilderness of Paran at Kadesh. They brought back a report for the whole congregation and showed them the fruit of the land.
units.rightText: And they went and came to Moses, and to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, unto the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and brought back word unto them, and unto all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.

units.leftText: And they gave this account to Moses: “We went into the land to which you sent us, and indeed, it is flowing with milk and honey. Here is some of its fruit!
units.rightText: And they told him, and said, We came unto the land whither thou sentest us; and surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, the people living in the land are strong, and the cities are large and fortified. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
units.rightText: Howbeit the people that dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.

units.leftText: The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”
units.rightText: Amalek dwelleth in the land of the South: and the Hittite, and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, dwell in the hill-country; and the Canaanite dwelleth by the sea, and along by the side of the Jordan.

units.leftText: Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!”
units.rightText: And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.

units.leftText: But the men who had gone up with him replied, “We cannot go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are!”
units.rightText: But the men that went up with him said, We are not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.

units.leftText: So they gave the Israelites a bad report about the land that they had spied out: “The land we explored devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw there are great in stature.
units.rightText: And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had spied out unto the children of Israel, saying, The land, through which we have gone to spy it out, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of great stature.

units.leftText: We even saw the Nephilim there— the descendants of Anak that come from the Nephilim! We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight, and we must have seemed the same to them!”
units.rightText: And there we saw the Nephilim, the sons of Anak, who come of the Nephilim: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.

units.leftText: Then the whole congregation lifted up their voices and cried out, and that night the people wept.
units.rightText: And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.

units.leftText: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!
units.rightText: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: and the whole congregation said unto them, Would that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would that we had died in this wilderness!

units.leftText: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?”
units.rightText: And wherefore doth Jehovah bring us unto this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will be a prey: were it not better for us to return into Egypt?

units.leftText: So they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”
units.rightText: And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.

units.leftText: Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel.
units.rightText: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes
units.rightText: And Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who were of them that spied out the land, rent their clothes:

units.leftText: and said to the whole congregation of Israel, “The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.
units.rightText: and they spake unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to spy it out, is an exceeding good land.

units.leftText: If the LORD delights in us, He will bring us into this land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and He will give it to us.
units.rightText: If Jehovah delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it unto us; a land which floweth with milk and honey.

units.leftText: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they will be like bread for us. Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!”
units.rightText: Only rebel not against Jehovah, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is removed from over them, and Jehovah is with us: fear them not.

units.leftText: But the whole congregation threatened to stone Joshua and Caleb.
units.rightText: But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of Jehovah appeared in the tent of meeting unto all the children of Israel.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, How long will this people despise me? and how long will they not believe in me, for all the signs which I have wrought among them?

units.leftText: I will strike them with a plague and destroy them — and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are.” Moses Intercedes for Israel
units.rightText: I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a nation greater and mightier than they.

units.leftText: But Moses said to the LORD, “The Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your strength You brought this people from among them.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Jehovah, Then the Egyptians will hear it; for thou broughtest up this people in thy might from among them;

units.leftText: And they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have already heard that You, O LORD, are in the midst of this people, that You, O LORD, have been seen face to face, that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
units.rightText: and they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that thou Jehovah art in the midst of this people; for thou Jehovah art seen face to face, and thy cloud standeth over them, and thou goest before them, in a pillar of cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night.

units.leftText: If You kill this people as one man, the nations who have heard of Your fame will say,
units.rightText: Now if thou shalt kill this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of thee will speak, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Because the LORD was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to give them, He has slaughtered them in the wilderness.’
units.rightText: Because Jehovah was not able to bring this people into the land which he sware unto them, therefore he hath slain them in the wilderness.

units.leftText: So now I pray, may the power of my Lord be magnified, just as You have declared:
units.rightText: And now, I pray thee, let the power of the Lord be great, according as thou hast spoken, saying,

units.leftText: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion, forgiving iniquity and transgression. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generation.’
units.rightText: Jehovah is slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness, forgiving iniquity and transgression; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation.
leftNotes: 14:18 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion, just as You have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.” God’s Forgiveness and Judgment (Deuteronomy 1:34–40|DEU 1:34-40*)
units.rightText: Pardon, I pray thee, the iniquity of this people according unto the greatness of thy lovingkindness, and according as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.

units.leftText: “I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, I have pardoned according to thy word:

units.leftText: “Yet as surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD,
units.rightText: but in very deed, as I live, and as all the earth shall be filled with the glory of Jehovah;

units.leftText: not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness — yet have tested Me and disobeyed Me these ten times —
units.rightText: because all those men that have seen my glory, and my signs, which I wrought in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tempted me these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice;

units.leftText: not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers. None of those who have treated Me with contempt will see it.
units.rightText: surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that despised me see it:

units.leftText: But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he has entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
units.rightText: but my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.

units.leftText: Now since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea. ”
units.rightText: Now the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valley: to-morrow turn ye, and get you into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.
leftNotes: 14:25 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

units.leftText: “How long will this wicked congregation grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints that the Israelites are making against Me.
units.rightText: How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, that murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me.

units.leftText: So tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly as I heard you say.
units.rightText: Say unto them, As I live, saith Jehovah, surely as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you:

units.leftText: Your bodies will fall in this wilderness— all who were numbered in the census, everyone twenty years of age or older— because you have grumbled against Me.
units.rightText: your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, that have murmured against me,

units.leftText: Surely none of you will enter the land in which I swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
units.rightText: surely ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware that I would make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.

units.leftText: But I will bring your children, whom you said would become plunder, into the land you have rejected — and they will enjoy it.
units.rightText: But your little ones, that ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have rejected.

units.leftText: As for you, however, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
units.rightText: But as for you, your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness.

units.leftText: Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, and they will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.
units.rightText: And your children shall be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your whoredoms, until your dead bodies be consumed in the wilderness.

units.leftText: In keeping with the forty days you spied out the land, you shall bear your guilt forty years — a year for each day — and you will experience My alienation.
units.rightText: After the number of the days in which ye spied out the land, even forty days, for every day a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years, and ye shall know my alienation.

units.leftText: I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this entire wicked congregation, which has conspired against Me. They will meet their end in the wilderness, and there they will die.” The Plague on the Ten Spies
units.rightText: I, Jehovah, have spoken, surely this will I do unto all this evil congregation, that are gathered together against me: in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.

units.leftText: So the men Moses had sent to spy out the land, who had returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing out a bad report about the land—
units.rightText: And the men, whom Moses sent to spy out the land, who returned, and made all the congregation to murmur against him, by bringing up an evil report against the land,

units.leftText: those men who had brought out the bad report about the land— were struck down by a plague before the LORD.
units.rightText: even those men that did bring up an evil report of the land, died by the plague before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Of those men who had gone to spy out the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
units.rightText: But Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, remained alive of those men that went to spy out the land.

units.leftText: And when Moses relayed these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly. The Defeat at Hormah (Deuteronomy 1:41–46|DEU 1:41-46*)
units.rightText: And Moses told these words unto all the children of Israel: and the people mourned greatly.

units.leftText: Early the next morning they got up and went up toward the ridge of the hill country. “We have indeed sinned,” they said, “but we will go to the place the LORD has promised.”
units.rightText: And they rose up early in the morning, and gat them up to the top of the mountain, saying, Lo, we are here, and will go up unto the place which Jehovah hath promised: for we have sinned.

units.leftText: But Moses said, “Why are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? This will not succeed!
units.rightText: And Moses said, Wherefore now do ye transgress the commandment of Jehovah, seeing it shall not prosper?

units.leftText: Do not go up, lest you be struck down by your enemies, because the LORD is not among you.
units.rightText: Go not up, for Jehovah is not among you; that ye be not smitten down before your enemies.

units.leftText: For there the Amalekites and Canaanites will face you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, He will not be with you.”
units.rightText: For there the Amalekite and the Canaanite are before you, and ye shall fall by the sword: because ye are turned back from following Jehovah, therefore Jehovah will not be with you.

units.leftText: But they dared to go up to the ridge of the hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the covenant of the LORD moved from the camp.
units.rightText: But they presumed to go up to the top of the mountain: nevertheless the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, and Moses, departed not out of the camp.

units.leftText: Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that part of the hill country came down, attacked them, and routed them all the way to Hormah.
units.rightText: Then the Amalekite came down, and the Canaanite who dwelt in that mountain, and smote them and beat them down, even unto Hormah.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: After you enter the land that I am giving you as a home
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye are come into the land of your habitations, which I give unto you,

units.leftText: and you present a food offering to the LORD from the herd or flock to produce a pleasing aroma to the LORD — either a burnt offering or a sacrifice, for a special vow or freewill offering or appointed feast—
units.rightText: and will make an offering by fire unto Jehovah, a burnt-offering, or a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or as a freewill-offering, or in your set feasts, to make a sweet savor unto Jehovah, of the herd, or of the flock;

units.leftText: then the one presenting his offering to the LORD shall also present a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of olive oil.
units.rightText: then shall he that offereth his oblation offer unto Jehovah a meal-offering of a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour mingled with the fourth part of a hin of oil:
leftNotes: 15:4 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour).
15:4 Or a quarter hin of oil; that is, approximately 0.97 quarts or 0.92 liters; similarly in verse 5

units.leftText: With the burnt offering or sacrifice of each lamb, you are to prepare a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering.
units.rightText: and wine for the drink-offering, the fourth part of a hin, shalt thou prepare with the burnt-offering, or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.

units.leftText: With a ram you are to prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of olive oil,
units.rightText: Or for a ram, thou shalt prepare for a meal-offering two tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour mingled with the third part of a hin of oil:
leftNotes: 15:6 Two-tenths of an ephah is approximately 4 dry quarts or 4.4 liters (probably about 5.1 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of flour).
15:6 Or a third of a hin of oil; that is, approximately 1.3 quarts or 1.2 liters; similarly in verse 7

units.leftText: and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: and for the drink-offering thou shalt offer the third part of a hin of wine, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,
units.rightText: And when thou preparest a bullock for a burnt-offering, or for a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or for peace-offerings unto Jehovah;

units.leftText: present with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of olive oil.
units.rightText: then shall he offer with the bullock a meal-offering of three tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour mingled with half a hin of oil:
leftNotes: 15:9 Three-tenths of an ephah is approximately 6 dry quarts or 6.6 liters (probably about 7.6 pounds or 3.5 kilograms of flour).
15:9 Or half a hin of oil; that is, approximately 1.9 quarts or 1.8 liters; similarly in verse 10

units.leftText: Also present half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: and thou shalt offer for the drink-offering half a hin of wine, for an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is to be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.
units.rightText: Thus shall it be done for each bullock, or for each ram, or for each of the he-lambs, or of the kids.

units.leftText: This is how you must prepare each one, no matter how many.
units.rightText: According to the number that ye shall prepare, so shall ye do to every one according to their number.

units.leftText: Everyone who is native-born shall prepare these things in this way when he presents a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: All that are home-born shall do these things after this manner, in offering an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And for the generations to come, if a foreigner residing with you or someone else among you wants to prepare a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he is to do exactly as you do.
units.rightText: And if a stranger sojourn with you, or whosoever may be among you throughout your generations, and will offer an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah; as ye do, so he shall do.

units.leftText: The assembly is to have the same statute both for you and for the foreign resident; it is a permanent statute for the generations to come. You and the foreigner shall be the same before the LORD.
units.rightText: For the assembly, there shall be one statute for you, and for the stranger that sojourneth with you, a statute for ever throughout your generations: as ye are, so shall the sojourner be before Jehovah.

units.leftText: The same law and the same ordinance will apply both to you and to the foreigner residing with you.”
units.rightText: One law and one ordinance shall be for you, and for the stranger that sojourneth with you.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land whither I bring you,

units.leftText: and you eat the food of the land, you shall lift up an offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: then it shall be, that, when ye eat of the bread of the land, ye shall offer up a heave-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: From the first of your dough, you are to lift up a cake as a contribution; offer it just like an offering from the threshing floor.
units.rightText: Of the first of your dough ye shall offer up a cake for a heave-offering: as the heave-offering of the threshing-floor, so shall ye heave it.

units.leftText: Throughout your generations, you are to give the LORD an offering from the first of your dough. Offerings for Unintentional Sins
units.rightText: Of the first of your dough ye shall give unto Jehovah a heave-offering throughout your generations.

units.leftText: Now if you stray unintentionally and do not obey all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses—
units.rightText: And when ye shall err, and not observe all these commandments, which Jehovah hath spoken unto Moses,

units.leftText: all that the LORD has commanded you through Moses from the day the LORD gave them and continuing through the generations to come—
units.rightText: even all that Jehovah hath commanded you by Moses, from the day that Jehovah gave commandment, and onward throughout your generations;

units.leftText: and if it was done unintentionally without the knowledge of the congregation, then the whole congregation is to prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the regulation, and one male goat as a sin offering.
units.rightText: then it shall be, if it be done unwittingly, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one young bullock for a burnt-offering, for a sweet savor unto Jehovah, with the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof, according to the ordinance, and one he-goat for a sin-offering.

units.leftText: The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, so that they may be forgiven; for the sin was unintentional and they have brought to the LORD a food offering and a sin offering, presented before the LORD for their unintentional sin.
units.rightText: And the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and they shall be forgiven; for it was an error, and they have brought their oblation, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah, and their sin-offering before Jehovah, for their error:

units.leftText: Then the whole congregation of Israel and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.
units.rightText: and all the congregation of the children of Israel shall be forgiven, and the stranger that sojourneth among them; for in respect of all the people it was done unwittingly.

units.leftText: Also, if one person sins unintentionally, he is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
units.rightText: And if one person sin unwittingly, then he shall offer a she-goat a year old for a sin-offering.

units.leftText: And the priest shall make atonement before the LORD on behalf of the person who erred by sinning unintentionally; and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.
units.rightText: And the priest shall make atonement for the soul that erreth, when he sinneth unwittingly, before Jehovah, to make atonement for him; and he shall be forgiven.

units.leftText: You shall have the same law for the one who acts in error, whether he is a native-born Israelite or a foreigner residing among you.
units.rightText: Ye shall have one law for him that doeth aught unwittingly, for him that is home-born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.

units.leftText: But the person who sins defiantly, whether a native or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD. That person shall be cut off from among his people.
units.rightText: But the soul that doeth aught with a high hand, whether he be home-born or a sojourner, the same blasphemeth Jehovah; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people.

units.leftText: He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment; his guilt remains on him.” A Sabbath-Breaker Stoned (Exodus 31:12–17|EXO 31:12-17*)
units.rightText: Because he hath despised the word of Jehovah, and hath broken his commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off; his iniquity shall be upon him.

units.leftText: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
units.rightText: And while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks upon the sabbath day.

units.leftText: Those who found the man gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation,
units.rightText: And they that found him gathering sticks brought him unto Moses and Aaron, and unto all the congregation.

units.leftText: and because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody.
units.rightText: And they put him in ward, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, The man shall surely be put to death: all the congregation shall stone him with stones without the camp.

units.leftText: So the whole congregation took the man outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses. The Law of Tassels
units.rightText: And all the congregation brought him without the camp, and stoned him to death with stones; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that throughout the generations to come they are to make for themselves tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of each border a cord of blue:

units.leftText: These will serve as tassels for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD, that you may obey them and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes.
units.rightText: and it shall be unto you for a fringe, that ye may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of Jehovah, and do them; and that ye follow not after your own heart and your own eyes, after which ye use to play the harlot;

units.leftText: Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God.
units.rightText: that ye may remember and do all my commandments, and be holy unto your God.

units.leftText: I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: I am Jehovah your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: Now Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath son of Levi, along with some Reubenites — Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth — conducted
units.rightText: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took men:

units.leftText: a rebellion against Moses, along with 250 men of Israel renowned as leaders of the congregation and representatives in the assembly.
units.rightText: and they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the congregation, called to the assembly, men of renown;

units.leftText: They came together against Moses and Aaron and told them, “You have taken too much upon yourselves! For everyone in the entire congregation is holy, and the LORD is in their midst. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
units.rightText: and they assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said unto them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and Jehovah is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the assembly of Jehovah?
leftNotes: 16:3 Figuratively You have gone too far or You have appropriated too much authority to yourselves; similarly in verse 7

units.leftText: When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.
units.rightText: And when Moses heard it, he fell upon his face:

units.leftText: Then he said to Korah and all his followers, “Tomorrow morning the LORD will reveal who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He will bring that person near to Himself. The one He chooses He will bring near to Himself.
units.rightText: and he spake unto Korah and unto all his company, saying, In the morning Jehovah will show who are his, and who is holy, and will cause him to come near unto him: even him whom he shall choose will he cause to come near unto him.
leftNotes: 16:5 LXX God has visited and knows those who are His; cited in 2 Timothy 2:19|2TI 2:19*
