units.leftText: You, Korah, and all your followers are to do as follows: Take censers,
units.rightText: This do: take you censers, Korah, and all his company;

units.leftText: and tomorrow you are to place fire and incense in them in the presence of the LORD. Then the man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. It is you sons of Levi who have taken too much upon yourselves!”
units.rightText: and put fire in them, and put incense upon them before Jehovah to-morrow: and it shall be that the man whom Jehovah doth choose, he shall be holy: ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.

units.leftText: Moses also said to Korah, “Now listen, you sons of Levi!
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Korah, Hear now, ye sons of Levi:

units.leftText: Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel and brought you near to Himself to perform the work at the LORD’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
units.rightText: seemeth it but a small thing unto you, that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle of Jehovah, and to stand before the congregation to minister unto them;

units.leftText: He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites, but you are seeking the priesthood as well.
units.rightText: and that he hath brought thee near, and all thy brethren the sons of Levi with thee? and seek ye the priesthood also?

units.leftText: Therefore, it is you and all your followers who have conspired against the LORD! As for Aaron, who is he that you should grumble against him?”
units.rightText: Therefore thou and all thy company are gathered together against Jehovah: and Aaron, what is he that ye murmur against him?

units.leftText: Then Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come!
units.rightText: And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab; and they said, We will not come up:

units.leftText: Is it not enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also appoint yourself as ruler over us?
units.rightText: is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, but thou must needs make thyself also a prince over us?

units.leftText: Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? No, we will not come!”
units.rightText: Moreover thou hast not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us inheritance of fields and vineyards: wilt thou put out the eyes of these men? we will not come up.

units.leftText: Then Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, “Do not regard their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them or mistreated a single one of them.”
units.rightText: And Moses was very wroth, and said unto Jehovah, Respect not thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I hurt one of them.

units.leftText: And Moses said to Korah, “You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow— you and they and Aaron.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Korah, Be thou and all thy company before Jehovah, thou, and they, and Aaron, to-morrow:

units.leftText: Each man is to take his censer, place incense in it, and present it before the LORD— 250 censers. You and Aaron are to present your censers as well.”
units.rightText: and take ye every man his censer, and put incense upon them, and bring ye before Jehovah every man his censer, two hundred and fifty censers; thou also, and Aaron, each his censer.

units.leftText: So each man took his censer, put fire and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And they took every man his censer, and put fire in them, and laid incense thereon, and stood at the door of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.

units.leftText: When Korah had gathered his whole assembly against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.
units.rightText: And Korah assembled all the congregation against them unto the door of the tent of meeting: and the glory of Jehovah appeared unto all the congregation.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

units.leftText: “Separate yourselves from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.”
units.rightText: Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.

units.leftText: But Moses and Aaron fell facedown and said, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, when one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?” Moses Separates the People
units.rightText: And they fell upon their faces, and said, O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation?

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell the congregation to move away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
units.rightText: Speak unto the congregation, saying, Get you up from about the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.

units.leftText: So Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
units.rightText: And Moses rose up and went unto Dathan and Abiram; and the elders of Israel followed him.

units.leftText: And he warned the congregation, “Move away now from the tents of these wicked men. Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins.”
units.rightText: And he spake unto the congregation, saying, Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest ye be consumed in all their sins.

units.leftText: So they moved away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Meanwhile, Dathan and Abiram had come out and stood at the entrances to their tents with their wives and children and infants. The Earth Swallows Korah
units.rightText: So they gat them up from the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, on every side: and Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood at the door of their tents, and their wives, and their sons, and their little ones.

units.leftText: Then Moses said, “This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things, for it was not my own doing:
units.rightText: And Moses said, Hereby ye shall know that Jehovah hath sent me to do all these works; for I have not done them of mine own mind.

units.leftText: If these men die a natural death, or if they suffer the fate of all men, then the LORD has not sent me.
units.rightText: If these men die the common death of all men, or if they be visited after the visitation of all men; then Jehovah hath not sent me.

units.leftText: But if the LORD brings about something unprecedented, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them so that they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt.”
units.rightText: But if Jehovah make a new thing, and the ground open its mouth, and swallow them up, with all that appertain unto them, and they go down alive into Sheol; then ye shall understand that these men have despised Jehovah.

units.leftText: As soon as Moses had finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground clave asunder that was under them;

units.leftText: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households — all Korah’s men and all their possessions.
units.rightText: and the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.

units.leftText: They went down alive into Sheol with all they owned. The earth closed over them, and they vanished from the assembly.
units.rightText: So they, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into Sheol: and the earth closed upon them, and they perished from among the assembly.

units.leftText: At their cries, all the people of Israel who were around them fled, saying, “The earth may swallow us too!”
units.rightText: And all Israel that were round about them fled at the cry of them; for they said, Lest the earth swallow us up.

units.leftText: And fire came forth from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense. The Censers Reserved for Holy Use
units.rightText: And fire came forth from Jehovah, and devoured the two hundred and fifty men that offered the incense.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to remove the censers from the flames and to scatter the coals far away, because the censers are holy.
units.rightText: Speak unto Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter thou the fire yonder; for they are holy,

units.leftText: As for the censers of those who sinned at the cost of their own lives, hammer them into sheets to overlay the altar, for these were presented before the LORD, and so have become holy. They will serve as a sign to the Israelites.”
units.rightText: even the censers of these sinners against their own lives; and let them be made beaten plates for a covering of the altar: for they offered them before Jehovah; therefore they are holy; and they shall be a sign unto the children of Israel.

units.leftText: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers brought by those who had been burned up, and he had them hammered out to overlay the altar,
units.rightText: And Eleazar the priest took the brazen censers, which they that were burnt had offered; and they beat them out for a covering of the altar,

units.leftText: just as the LORD commanded him through Moses. This was to be a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to offer incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his followers. Murmuring and Plague (1 Corinthians 10:1–13|1CO 10:1-13*)
units.rightText: to be a memorial unto the children of Israel, to the end that no stranger, that is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to burn incense before Jehovah; that he be not as Korah, and as his company: as Jehovah spake unto him by Moses.

units.leftText: The next day the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the LORD’s people!”
units.rightText: But on the morrow all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, Ye have killed the people of Jehovah.

units.leftText: But when the congregation gathered against them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the Tent of Meeting, and suddenly the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the congregation was assembled against Moses and against Aaron, that they looked toward the tent of meeting: and, behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of Jehovah appeared.

units.leftText: Then Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting,
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: and the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Get away from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.” And Moses and Aaron fell facedown.
units.rightText: Get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment. And they fell upon their faces.

units.leftText: Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer, place fire from the altar in it, and add incense. Go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, because wrath has come out from the LORD; the plague has begun.”
units.rightText: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take thy censer, and put fire therein from off the altar, and lay incense thereon, and carry it quickly unto the congregation, and make atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from Jehovah; the plague is begun.

units.leftText: So Aaron took the censer as Moses had ordered and ran into the midst of the assembly. And seeing that the plague had begun among the people, he offered the incense and made atonement for the people.
units.rightText: And Aaron took as Moses spake, and ran into the midst of the assembly; and, behold, the plague was begun among the people: and he put on the incense, and made atonement for the people.

units.leftText: He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague was halted.
units.rightText: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.

units.leftText: But those who died from the plague numbered 14,700, in addition to those who had died on account of Korah.
units.rightText: Now they that died by the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, besides them that died about the matter of Korah.

units.leftText: Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, since the plague had been halted.
units.rightText: And Aaron returned unto Moses unto the door of the tent of meeting: and the plague was stayed.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the Israelites and take from them twelve staffs, one from the leader of each tribe. Write each man’s name on his staff,
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, and take of them rods, one for each fathers’ house, of all their princes according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods: write thou every man’s name upon his rod.

units.leftText: and write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi, because there must be one staff for the head of each tribe.
units.rightText: And thou shalt write Aaron’s name upon the rod of Levi; for there shall be one rod for each head of their fathers’ houses.

units.leftText: Place the staffs in the Tent of Meeting in front of the Testimony, where I meet with you.
units.rightText: And thou shalt lay them up in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
leftNotes: 17:4 The Testimony refers to the stone tablets in the ark of the covenant inscribed with the Ten Commandments; also in verse 10.

units.leftText: The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid Myself of the constant grumbling of the Israelites against you.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that the rod of the man whom I shall choose shall bud: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against you.

units.leftText: So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders gave him a staff — one for each of the leaders of their tribes, twelve staffs in all. And Aaron’s staff was among them.
units.rightText: And Moses spake unto the children of Israel; and all their princes gave him rods, for each prince one, according to their fathers’ houses, even twelve rods: and the rod of Aaron was among their rods.

units.leftText: Then Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony.
units.rightText: And Moses laid up the rods before Jehovah in the tent of the testimony.

units.leftText: The next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony and saw that Aaron’s staff, representing the house of Levi, had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed, and produced almonds.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses went into the tent of the testimony; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and put forth buds, and produced blossoms, and bare ripe almonds.

units.leftText: Then Moses brought out all the staffs from the LORD’s presence to all the Israelites. They saw them, and each man took his own staff.
units.rightText: And Moses brought out all the rods from before Jehovah unto all the children of Israel: and they looked, and took every man his rod.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious, so that you may put an end to their grumbling against Me, lest they die.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Put back the rod of Aaron before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the children of rebellion; that thou mayest make an end of their murmurings against me, that they die not.

units.leftText: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: Thus did Moses: as Jehovah commanded him, so did he.

units.leftText: Then the Israelites declared to Moses, “Look, we are perishing! We are lost; we are all lost!
units.rightText: And the children of Israel spake unto Moses, saying, Behold, we perish, we are undone, we are all undone.

units.leftText: Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die. Are we all going to perish?”
units.rightText: Every one that cometh near, that cometh near unto the tabernacle of Jehovah, dieth: shall we perish all of us?

units.leftText: So the LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your father’s house must bear the iniquity involving the sanctuary. And you and your sons alone must bear the iniquity involving your priesthood.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Aaron, Thou and thy sons and thy fathers’ house with thee shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and thou and thy sons with thee shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.

units.leftText: But bring with you also your brothers from the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, that they may join you and assist you and your sons before the Tent of the Testimony.
units.rightText: And thy brethren also, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of thy father, bring thou near with thee, that they may be joined unto thee, and minister unto thee: but thou and thy sons with thee shall be before the tent of the testimony.

units.leftText: And they shall attend to your duties and to all the duties of the Tent; but they must not come near to the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, or both they and you will die.
units.rightText: And they shall keep thy charge, and the charge of all the Tent: only they shall not come nigh unto the vessels of the sanctuary and unto the altar, that they die not, neither they, nor ye.

units.leftText: They are to join you and attend to the duties of the Tent of Meeting, doing all the work at the Tent; but no outsider may come near you.
units.rightText: And they shall be joined unto thee, and keep the charge of the tent of meeting, for all the service of the Tent: and a stranger shall not come nigh unto you.

units.leftText: And you shall attend to the duties of the sanctuary and of the altar, so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again.
units.rightText: And ye shall keep the charge of the sanctuary, and the charge of the altar; that there be wrath no more upon the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Behold, I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites as a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD to perform the service for the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And I, behold, I have taken your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel: to you they are a gift, given unto Jehovah, to do the service of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: But only you and your sons shall attend to your priesthood for everything concerning the altar and what is inside the veil, and you are to perform that service. I am giving you the work of the priesthood as a gift, but any outsider who comes near the sanctuary must be put to death.” Offerings for Priests and Levites
units.rightText: And thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priesthood for everything of the altar, and for that within the veil; and ye shall serve: I give you the priesthood as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Aaron, “Behold, I have put you in charge of My offerings. As for all the sacred offerings of the Israelites, I have given them to you and your sons as a portion and a permanent statute.
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Aaron, And I, behold, I have given thee the charge of my heave-offerings, even all the hallowed things of the children of Israel; unto thee have I given them by reason of the anointing, and to thy sons, as a portion for ever.

units.leftText: A portion of the most holy offerings reserved from the fire will be yours. From all the offerings they render to Me as most holy offerings, whether grain offerings or sin offerings or guilt offerings, that part belongs to you and your sons.
units.rightText: This shall be thine of the most holy things, reserved from the fire: every oblation of theirs, even every meal-offering of theirs, and every sin-offering of theirs, and every trespass-offering of theirs, which they shall render unto me, shall be most holy for thee and for thy sons.

units.leftText: You are to eat it as a most holy offering, and every male may eat it. You shall regard it as holy.
units.rightText: As the most holy things shalt thou eat thereof; every male shall eat thereof: it shall be holy unto thee.
leftNotes: 18:10 Or You are to eat it in a most holy place

units.leftText: And this is yours as well: the offering of their gifts, along with all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given this to you and your sons and daughters as a permanent statute. Every ceremonially clean person in your household may eat it.
units.rightText: And this is thine: the heave-offering of their gift, even all the wave-offerings of the children of Israel; I have given them unto thee, and to thy sons and to thy daughters with thee, as a portion for ever; every one that is clean in thy house shall eat thereof.

units.leftText: I give you all the freshest olive oil and all the finest new wine and grain that the Israelites give to the LORD as their firstfruits.
units.rightText: All the best of the oil, and all the best of the vintage, and of the grain, the first-fruits of them which they give unto Jehovah, to thee have I given them.

units.leftText: The firstfruits of everything in their land that they bring to the LORD will belong to you. Every ceremonially clean person in your household may eat them.
units.rightText: The first-ripe fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring unto Jehovah, shall be thine; every one that is clean in thy house shall eat thereof.

units.leftText: Every devoted thing in Israel belongs to you.
units.rightText: Everything devoted in Israel shall be thine.

units.leftText: The firstborn of every womb, whether man or beast, that is offered to the LORD belongs to you. But you must surely redeem every firstborn son and every firstborn male of unclean animals.
units.rightText: Everything that openeth the womb, of all flesh which they offer unto Jehovah, both of man and beast shall be thine: nevertheless the first-born of man shalt thou surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shalt thou redeem.

units.leftText: You are to pay the redemption price for a month-old male according to your valuation: five shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
units.rightText: And those that are to be redeemed of them from a month old shalt thou redeem, according to thine estimation, for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary (the same is twenty gerahs).
leftNotes: 18:16 5 shekels is approximately 2 ounces or 57 grams of silver.
18:16 20 gerahs is equivalent to one shekel (approximately 0.4 ounces or 11.4 grams).

units.leftText: But you must not redeem the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat; they are holy. You are to splatter their blood on the altar and burn their fat as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: But the firstling of a cow, or the firstling of a sheep, or the firstling of a goat, thou shalt not redeem; they are holy: thou shalt sprinkle their blood upon the altar, and shalt burn their fat for an offering made by fire, for a sweet savor unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And their meat belongs to you, just as the breast and right thigh of the wave offering belong to you.
units.rightText: And the flesh of them shall be thine, as the wave-breast and as the right thigh, it shall be thine.

units.leftText: All the holy offerings that the Israelites present to the LORD I give to you and to your sons and daughters as a permanent statute. It is a permanent covenant of salt before the LORD for you and your offspring.”
units.rightText: All the heave-offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer unto Jehovah, have I given thee, and thy sons and thy daughters with thee, as a portion for ever: it is a covenant of salt for ever before Jehovah unto thee and to thy seed with thee.
leftNotes: 18:19 That is, a perpetual covenant

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Aaron, Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any portion among them: I am thy portion and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Behold, I have given to the Levites all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance in return for the work they do, the service of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And unto the children of Levi, behold, I have given all the tithe in Israel for an inheritance, in return for their service which they serve, even the service of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: No longer may the Israelites come near to the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die.
units.rightText: And henceforth the children of Israel shall not come nigh the tent of meeting, lest they bear sin, and die.

units.leftText: The Levites are to perform the work of the Tent of Meeting, and they must bear their iniquity. This is a permanent statute for the generations to come. The Levites will not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.
units.rightText: But the Levites shall do the service of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations; and among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance.

units.leftText: For I have given to the Levites as their inheritance the tithe that the Israelites present to the LORD as a contribution. That is why I told them that they would not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.”
units.rightText: For the tithe of the children of Israel, which they offer as a heave-offering unto Jehovah, I have given to the Levites for an inheritance: therefore I have said unto them, Among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance.

units.leftText: And the LORD instructed Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the Levites and tell them: ‘When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you as your inheritance, you must present part of it as an offering to the LORD— a tithe of the tithe.
units.rightText: Moreover thou shalt speak unto the Levites, and say unto them, When ye take of the children of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for your inheritance, then ye shall offer up a heave-offering of it for Jehovah, a tithe of the tithe.

units.leftText: Your offering will be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor or juice from the winepress.
units.rightText: And your heave-offering shall be reckoned unto you, as though it were the grain of the threshing-floor, and as the fulness of the winepress.

units.leftText: So you are to present an offering to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites, and from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest.
units.rightText: Thus ye also shall offer a heave-offering unto Jehovah of all your tithes, which ye receive of the children of Israel; and thereof ye shall give Jehovah’s heave-offering to Aaron the priest.

units.leftText: You must present the offering due the LORD from all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it.’
units.rightText: Out of all your gifts ye shall offer every heave-offering of Jehovah, of all the best thereof, even the hallowed part thereof out of it.

units.leftText: Therefore say to the Levites, ‘When you have presented the best part, it will be reckoned to you as the produce of the threshing floor or winepress.
units.rightText: Therefore thou shalt say unto them, When ye heave the best thereof from it, then it shall be reckoned unto the Levites as the increase of the threshing-floor, and as the increase of the winepress.

units.leftText: And you and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere; it is the compensation for your work at the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And ye shall eat it in every place, ye and your households: for it is your reward in return for your service in the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: Once you have presented the best part of it, you will not incur guilt because of it. But you must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, or else you will die.’”
units.rightText: And ye shall bear no sin by reason of it, when ye have heaved from it the best thereof: and ye shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, that ye die not.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

units.leftText: “This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Instruct the Israelites to bring you an unblemished red heifer that has no defect and has never been placed under a yoke.
units.rightText: This is the statute of the law which Jehovah hath commanded, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring thee a red heifer without spot, wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came yoke.

units.leftText: Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he will have it brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
units.rightText: And ye shall give her unto Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring her forth without the camp, and one shall slay her before his face:

units.leftText: Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: and Eleazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle her blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.

units.leftText: Then the heifer must be burned in his sight. Its hide, its flesh, and its blood are to be burned, along with its dung.
units.rightText: And one shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn:

units.leftText: The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet wool and throw them onto the burning heifer.
units.rightText: and the priest shall take cedar-wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.

units.leftText: Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; after that he may enter the camp, but he will be ceremonially unclean until evening.
units.rightText: Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: The one who burned the heifer must also wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he too will be ceremonially unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And he that burneth her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and store them in a ceremonially clean place outside the camp. They must be kept by the congregation of Israel for preparing the water of purification; this is for purification from sin.
units.rightText: And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up without the camp in a clean place; and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for a water for impurity: it is a sin-offering.

units.leftText: The man who has gathered up the ashes of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he will be ceremonially unclean until evening. This is a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them. Purification of the Unclean
units.rightText: And he that gathereth the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the even: and it shall be unto the children of Israel, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among them, for a statute for ever.

units.leftText: Whoever touches any dead body will be unclean for seven days.
units.rightText: He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days:

units.leftText: He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day; then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.
units.rightText: the same shall purify himself therewith on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean: but if he purify not himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean.

units.leftText: Anyone who touches a human corpse and fails to purify himself defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person must be cut off from Israel. He remains unclean, because the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, and his uncleanness is still on him.
units.rightText: Whosoever toucheth a dead person, the body of a man that hath died, and purifieth not himself, defileth the tabernacle of Jehovah; and that soul shall be cut off from Israel: because the water for impurity was not sprinkled upon him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness is yet upon him.

units.leftText: This is the law when a person dies in a tent: Everyone who enters the tent and everyone already in the tent will be unclean for seven days,
units.rightText: This is the law when a man dieth in a tent: every one that cometh into the tent, and every one that is in the tent, shall be unclean seven days.

units.leftText: and any open container without a lid fastened on it is unclean.
units.rightText: And every open vessel, which hath no covering bound upon it, is unclean.

units.leftText: Anyone in the open field who touches someone who has been killed by the sword or has died of natural causes, or anyone who touches a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
units.rightText: And whosoever in the open field toucheth one that is slain with a sword, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.

units.leftText: For the purification of the unclean person, take some of the ashes of the burnt sin offering, put them in a jar, and pour fresh water over them.
units.rightText: And for the unclean they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the sin-offering; and running water shall be put thereto in a vessel:
leftNotes: 19:17 Or flowing water or living water

units.leftText: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to take some hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the furnishings, and the people who were there. He is also to sprinkle the one who touched a bone, a grave, or a person who has died or been slain.
units.rightText: and a clean person shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the persons that were there, and upon him that touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave:

units.leftText: The man who is ceremonially clean is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. After he purifies the unclean person on the seventh day, the one being cleansed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and that evening he will be clean.
units.rightText: and the clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day: and on the seventh day he shall purify him; and he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at even.

units.leftText: But if a person who is unclean does not purify himself, he will be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
units.rightText: But the man that shall be unclean, and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he hath defiled the sanctuary of Jehovah: the water for impurity hath not been sprinkled upon him; he is unclean.

units.leftText: This is a permanent statute for the people: The one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And it shall be a perpetual statute unto them: and he that sprinkleth the water for impurity shall wash his clothes, and he that toucheth the water for impurity shall be unclean until even.

units.leftText: Anything the unclean person touches will become unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.”
units.rightText: And whatsoever the unclean person toucheth shall be unclean; and the soul that toucheth it shall be unclean until even.

units.leftText: In the first month, the whole congregation of Israel entered the Wilderness of Zin and stayed in Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month: and the people abode in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there.

units.leftText: Now there was no water for the congregation, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
units.rightText: And there was no water for the congregation: and they assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron.

units.leftText: The people quarreled with Moses and said, “If only we had perished with our brothers before the LORD!
units.rightText: And the people strove with Moses, and spake, saying, Would that we had died when our brethren died before Jehovah!

units.leftText: Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness for us and our livestock to die here?
units.rightText: And why have ye brought the assembly of Jehovah into this wilderness, that we should die there, we and our beasts?

units.leftText: Why have you led us up out of Egypt to bring us to this wretched place? It is not a place of grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates — and there is no water to drink!”
units.rightText: And wherefore have ye made us to come up out of Egypt, to bring us in unto this evil place? it is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.

units.leftText: Then Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. They fell facedown, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly unto the door of the tent of meeting, and fell upon their faces: and the glory of Jehovah appeared unto them.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Take the staff and assemble the congregation. You and your brother Aaron are to speak to the rock while they watch, and it will pour out its water. You will bring out water from the rock and provide drink for the congregation and their livestock.”
units.rightText: Take the rod, and assemble the congregation, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes, that it give forth its water; and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock; so thou shalt give the congregation and their cattle drink.

units.leftText: So Moses took the staff from the LORD’s presence, just as he had been commanded.
units.rightText: And Moses took the rod from before Jehovah, as he commanded him.

units.leftText: Then Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, “Listen now, you rebels, must we bring you water out of this rock?”
units.rightText: And Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; shall we bring you forth water out of this rock?

units.leftText: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff, so that a great amount of water gushed out, and the congregation and their livestock were able to drink.
units.rightText: And Moses lifted up his hand, and smote the rock with his rod twice: and water came forth abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their cattle.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed not in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.

units.leftText: These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He showed His holiness among them. Edom Refuses Passage
units.rightText: These are the waters of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with Jehovah, and he was sanctified in them.
leftNotes: 20:13 Meribah means quarreling; also in verse 24; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*.

units.leftText: From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to tell the king of Edom, “This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has befallen us,
units.rightText: And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:

units.leftText: how our fathers went down to Egypt, where we lived many years. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers,
units.rightText: how our fathers went down into Egypt, and we dwelt in Egypt a long time; and the Egyptians dealt ill with us, and our fathers:

units.leftText: and when we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt.
units.rightText: and when we cried unto Jehovah, he heard our voice, and sent an angel, and brought us forth out of Egypt: and, behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the uttermost of thy border.

units.leftText: Please let us pass through your land. We will not go through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway; we will not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”
units.rightText: Let us pass, I pray thee, through thy land: we will not pass through field or through vineyard, neither will we drink of the water of the wells; we will go along the king’s highway; we will not turn aside to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed thy border.

units.leftText: But Edom answered, “You may not travel through our land, or we will come out and confront you with the sword.”
units.rightText: And Edom said unto him, Thou shalt not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against thee.

units.leftText: “We will stay on the main road,” the Israelites replied, “and if we or our herds drink your water, we will pay for it. There will be no problem; only let us pass through on foot.”
units.rightText: And the children of Israel said unto him, We will go up by the highway; and if we drink of thy water, I and my cattle, then will I give the price thereof: let me only, without doing anything else, pass through on my feet.

units.leftText: But Edom insisted, “You may not pass through.” And they came out to confront the Israelites with a large army and a strong hand.
units.rightText: And he said, Thou shalt not pass through. And Edom came out against him with much people, and with a strong hand.

units.leftText: So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through their territory, and Israel turned away from them. The Death of Aaron
units.rightText: Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.

units.leftText: After they had set out from Kadesh, the whole congregation of Israel came to Mount Hor.
units.rightText: And they journeyed from Kadesh: and the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, came unto mount Hor.

units.leftText: And at Mount Hor, near the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and Aaron in mount Hor, by the border of the land of Edom, saying,

units.leftText: “Aaron will be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.
units.rightText: Aaron shall be gathered unto his people; for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the waters of Meribah.

units.leftText: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
units.rightText: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up unto mount Hor;

units.leftText: Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there.”
units.rightText: and strip Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son: and Aaron shall be gathered unto his people, and shall die there.

units.leftText: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded, and they climbed Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.
units.rightText: And Moses did as Jehovah commanded: and they went up into mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.

units.leftText: After Moses had removed Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar, Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
units.rightText: And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there on the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount.

units.leftText: When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days.
units.rightText: And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they wept for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.

units.leftText: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim, he attacked Israel and captured some prisoners.
units.rightText: And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the South, heard tell that Israel came by the way of Atharim; and he fought against Israel, and took some of them captive.

units.leftText: So Israel made a vow to the LORD: “If You will deliver this people into our hands, we will devote their cities to destruction. ”
units.rightText: And Israel vowed a vow unto Jehovah, and said, If thou wilt indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.
leftNotes: 21:2 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verse 3.

units.leftText: And the LORD heard Israel’s plea and delivered up the Canaanites. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction; so they named the place Hormah. The Bronze Serpent
units.rightText: And Jehovah hearkened to the voice of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites; and they utterly destroyed them and their cities: and the name of the place was called Hormah.
leftNotes: 21:3 Hormah means destruction.

units.leftText: Then they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea, in order to bypass the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the journey
units.rightText: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way to the Red Sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way.
leftNotes: 21:4 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: and spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you led us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and we detest this wretched food!”
units.rightText: And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, and there is no water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.

units.leftText: So the LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and many of the Israelites were bitten and died.
units.rightText: And Jehovah sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.

units.leftText: Then the people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Intercede with the LORD so He will take the snakes away from us.” So Moses interceded for the people.
units.rightText: And the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, because we have spoken against Jehovah, and against thee; pray unto Jehovah, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole. When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a standard: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he seeth it, shall live.

units.leftText: So Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live. The Journey to Moab
units.rightText: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and set it upon the standard: and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked unto the serpent of brass, he lived.

units.leftText: Then the Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel journeyed, and encamped in Oboth.

units.leftText: They journeyed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab to the east.
units.rightText: And they journeyed from Oboth, and encamped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrising.

units.leftText: From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.
units.rightText: From thence they journeyed, and encamped in the valley of Zered.

units.leftText: From there they moved on and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that extends into the Amorite territory.
units.rightText: From thence they journeyed, and encamped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness, that cometh out of the border of the Amorites: for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.

units.leftText: Therefore it is stated in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: “Waheb in Suphah and the wadis of the Arnon,
units.rightText: Wherefore it is said in the book of the Wars of Jehovah, Vaheb in Suphah, And the valleys of the Arnon,

units.leftText: even the slopes of the wadis that extend to the site of Ar and lie along the border of Moab.”
units.rightText: And the slope of the valleys That inclineth toward the dwelling of Ar, And leaneth upon the border of Moab.

units.leftText: From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people so that I may give them water.”
units.rightText: And from thence they journeyed to Beer: that is the well whereof Jehovah said unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water.
leftNotes: 21:16 Beer means well.

units.leftText: Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!
units.rightText: Then sang Israel this song: Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it:

units.leftText: The princes dug the well; the nobles of the people hollowed it out with their scepters and with their staffs.”
units.rightText: The well, which the princes digged, Which the nobles of the people delved, With the sceptre, and with their staves. And from the wilderness they journeyed to Mattanah;

units.leftText: and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
units.rightText: and from Mattanah to Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel to Bamoth;

units.leftText: and from Bamoth to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland. The Defeat of Sihon (Deuteronomy 2:24–37|DEU 2:24-37*)
units.rightText: and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looketh down upon the desert.
leftNotes: 21:20 Or Jeshimon

units.leftText: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
units.rightText: And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

units.leftText: “Let us pass through your land. We will not turn aside into any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”
units.rightText: Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn aside into field, or into vineyard; we will not drink of the water of the wells: we will go by the king’s highway, until we have passed thy border.

units.leftText: But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Instead, he gathered his whole army and went out to confront Israel in the wilderness. When he came to Jahaz, he fought against Israel.
units.rightText: And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness, and came to Jahaz; and he fought against Israel.
leftNotes: 21:23 Jahaz is a variant of Jahzah; see 1 Chronicles 6:78|1CH 6:78*.

units.leftText: And Israel put him to the sword and took possession of his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok — but only up to the border of the Ammonites, because it was fortified.
units.rightText: And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from the Arnon unto the Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon; for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
leftNotes: 21:24 Or because the territory was rugged; literally because it was strong

units.leftText: Israel captured all the cities of the Amorites and occupied them, including Heshbon and all its villages.
units.rightText: And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the towns thereof.

units.leftText: Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.
units.rightText: For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even unto the Arnon.

units.leftText: That is why the poets say: “Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored.
units.rightText: Wherefore they that speak in proverbs say, Come ye to Heshbon; Let the city of Sihon be built and established:

units.leftText: For a fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the rulers of Arnon’s heights.
units.rightText: For a fire is gone out of Heshbon, A flame from the city of Sihon: It hath devoured Ar of Moab, The lords of the high places of the Arnon.

units.leftText: Woe to you, O Moab! You are destroyed, O people of Chemosh! He gave up his sons as refugees, and his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.
units.rightText: Woe to thee, Moab! Thou art undone, O people of Chemosh: He hath given his sons as fugitives, And his daughters into captivity, Unto Sihon king of the Amorites.

units.leftText: But we have overthrown them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon. We demolished them as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba. ” The Defeat of Og (Deuteronomy 3:1–11|DEU 3:1-11*)
units.rightText: We have shot at them; Heshbon is perished even unto Dibon, And we have laid waste even unto Nophah, Which reacheth unto Medeba.
leftNotes: 21:30 Or We demolished them until fire spread to Medeba

units.leftText: So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
units.rightText: Thus Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites.

units.leftText: After Moses had sent spies to Jazer, Israel captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
units.rightText: And Moses sent to spy out Jazer; and they took the towns thereof, and drove out the Amorites that were there.

units.leftText: Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet them in battle at Edrei.
units.rightText: And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon.

units.leftText: So they struck down Og, along with his sons and his whole army, until no remnant was left. And they took possession of his land.
units.rightText: So they smote him, and his sons and all his people, until there was none left him remaining: and they possessed his land.

units.leftText: Then the Israelites traveled on and camped in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, across from Jericho.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel journeyed, and encamped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.

units.leftText: Now Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites,
units.rightText: And Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.

units.leftText: and Moab was terrified of the people because they were numerous. Indeed, Moab dreaded the Israelites.
units.rightText: And Moab was sore afraid of the people, because they were many: and Moab was distressed because of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: So the Moabites said to the elders of Midian, “This horde will devour everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.”
units.rightText: And Moab said unto the elders of Midian, Now will this multitude lick up all that is round about us, as the ox licketh up the grass of the field. And Balak the son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

units.leftText: he sent messengers to summon Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people.
units.rightText: And he sent messengers unto Balaam the son of Beor, to Pethor, which is by the River, to the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me.
leftNotes: 22:5 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: So please come now and put a curse on this people, because they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I may be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land; for I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.”
units.rightText: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: peradventure I shall prevail, that we may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land; for I know that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.

units.leftText: The elders of Moab and Midian departed with the fees for divination in hand. They came to Balaam and relayed to him the words of Balak.
units.rightText: And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand; and they came unto Balaam, and spake unto him the words of Balak.

units.leftText: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and I will give you the answer that the LORD speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Lodge here this night, and I will bring you word again, as Jehovah shall speak unto me: and the princes of Moab abode with Balaam.

units.leftText: Then God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men with you?”
units.rightText: And God came unto Balaam, and said, What men are these with thee?

units.leftText: And Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message:
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto God, Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent unto me, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Behold, a people has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps I may be able to fight against them and drive them away.’”
units.rightText: Behold, the people that is come out of Egypt, it covereth the face of the earth: now, come curse me them; peradventure I shall be able to fight against them, and shall drive them out.

units.leftText: But God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them. You are not to curse this people, for they are blessed.”
units.rightText: And God said unto Balaam, Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people; for they are blessed.

units.leftText: So Balaam got up the next morning and said to Balak’s princes, “Go back to your homeland, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you.”
units.rightText: And Balaam rose up in the morning, and said unto the princes of Balak, Get you into your land; for Jehovah refuseth to give me leave to go with you.

units.leftText: And the princes of Moab arose, returned to Balak, and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
units.rightText: And the princes of Moab rose up, and they went unto Balak, and said, Balaam refuseth to come with us.

units.leftText: Then Balak sent other princes, more numerous and more distinguished than the first messengers.
units.rightText: And Balak sent yet again princes, more, and more honorable than they.

units.leftText: They came to Balaam and said, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me,
units.rightText: And they came to Balaam, and said to him, Thus saith Balak the son of Zippor, Let nothing, I pray thee, hinder thee from coming unto me:

units.leftText: for I will honor you richly and do whatever you say. So please come and put a curse on this people for me!’”
units.rightText: for I will promote thee unto very great honor, and whatsoever thou sayest unto me I will do: come therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people.

units.leftText: But Balaam replied to the servants of Balak, “If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything small or great to go beyond the command of the LORD my God.
units.rightText: And Balaam answered and said unto the servants of Balak, If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of Jehovah my God, to do less or more.

units.leftText: So now, please stay here overnight as the others did, that I may find out what else the LORD has to tell me.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, I pray you, tarry ye also here this night, that I may know what Jehovah will speak unto me more.

units.leftText: That night God came to Balaam and said, “Since these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them, but you must only do what I tell you.”
units.rightText: And God came unto Balaam at night, and said unto him, If the men are come to call thee, rise up, go with them; but only the word which I speak unto thee, that shalt thou do.

units.leftText: So in the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab. The Angel and Balaam’s Donkey
units.rightText: And Balaam rose up in the morning, and saddled his ass, and went with the princes of Moab.

units.leftText: Then God’s anger was kindled because Balaam was going along, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
units.rightText: And God’s anger was kindled because he went; and the angel of Jehovah placed himself in the way for an adversary against him. Now he was riding upon his ass, and his two servants were with him.
leftNotes: 22:22 Or Angel; here through the rest of chapter 22; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.

units.leftText: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the path and went into a field. So Balaam beat her to return her to the path.
units.rightText: And the ass saw the angel of Jehovah standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the ass turned aside out of the way, and went into the field: and Balaam smote the ass, to turn her into the way.

units.leftText: Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow passage between two vineyards, with walls on either side.
units.rightText: Then the angel of Jehovah stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.

units.leftText: And the donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot against it. So he beat her once again.
units.rightText: And the ass saw the angel of Jehovah, and she thrust herself unto the wall, and crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall: and he smote her again.

units.leftText: And the angel of the LORD moved on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn to the right or left.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah went further, and stood in a narrow place, where was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.

units.leftText: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam, and he became furious and beat her with his staff.
units.rightText: And the ass saw the angel of Jehovah, and she lay down under Balaam: and Balaam’s anger was kindled, and he smote the ass with his staff.

units.leftText: Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”
units.rightText: And Jehovah opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?

units.leftText: Balaam answered the donkey, “You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now!”
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: I would there were a sword in my hand, for now I had killed thee.

units.leftText: But the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not the donkey you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?” “No,” he replied.
units.rightText: And the ass said unto Balaam, Am not I thine ass, upon which thou hast ridden all thy life long unto this day? was I ever wont to do so unto thee? and he said, Nay.

units.leftText: Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.
units.rightText: Then Jehovah opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of Jehovah standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and fell on his face.

units.leftText: The angel of the LORD asked him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto him, Wherefore hast thou smitten thine ass these three times? behold, I am come forth for an adversary, because thy way is perverse before me:
leftNotes: 22:32 Or reckless or contrary

units.leftText: The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away, then by now I would surely have killed you and let her live.”
units.rightText: and the ass saw me, and turned aside before me these three times: unless she had turned aside from me, surely now I had even slain thee, and saved her alive.

units.leftText: “I have sinned,” Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me. And now, if this is displeasing in your sight, I will go back home.”
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto the angel of Jehovah, I have sinned; for I knew not that thou stoodest in the way against me: now therefore, if it displease thee, I will get me back again.

units.leftText: But the angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but you are to speak only what I tell you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto Balaam, Go with the men; but only the word that I shall speak unto thee, that thou shalt speak. So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.

units.leftText: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.
units.rightText: And when Balak heard that Balaam was come, he went out to meet him unto the City of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, which is in the utmost part of the border.

units.leftText: And he said to Balaam, “Did I not send you an urgent summons? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to reward you richly?”
units.rightText: And Balak said unto Balaam, Did I not earnestly send unto thee to call thee? wherefore camest thou not unto me? am I not able indeed to promote thee to honor?

units.leftText: “See, I have come to you,” Balaam replied, “but can I say just anything? I must speak only the word that God puts in my mouth.”
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto Balak, Lo, I am come unto thee: have I now any power at all to speak anything? the word that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.

units.leftText: So Balaam accompanied Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
units.rightText: And Balaam went with Balak, and they came unto Kiriath-huzoth.

units.leftText: Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and he gave portions to Balaam and the princes who were with him.
units.rightText: And Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent to Balaam, and to the princes that were with him.

units.leftText: The next morning, Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see the outskirts of the camp of the people.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning, that Balak took Balaam, and brought him up into the high places of Baal; and he saw from thence the utmost part of the people.

units.leftText: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.

units.leftText: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
units.rightText: And Balak did as Balaam had spoken; and Balak and Balaam offered on every altar a bullock and a ram.

units.leftText: “Stay here by your burnt offering while I am gone,” Balaam said to Balak. “Perhaps the LORD will meet with me. And whatever He reveals to me, I will tell you.”
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto Balak, Stand by thy burnt-offering, and I will go: peradventure Jehovah will come to meet me; and whatsoever he showeth me I will tell thee. And he went to a bare height.

units.leftText: and God met with him. “I have set up seven altars,” Balaam said, “and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram.”
units.rightText: And God met Balaam: and he said unto him, I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.

units.leftText: Then the LORD put a message in Balaam’s mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and give him this message.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah put a word in Balaam’s mouth, and said, Return unto Balak, and thus thou shalt speak.

units.leftText: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there beside his burnt offering, with all the princes of Moab.
units.rightText: And he returned unto him, and, lo, he was standing by his burnt-offering, he, and all the princes of Moab.

units.leftText: And Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Balak brought me from Aram, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east. ‘Come,’ he said, ‘put a curse on Jacob for me; come and denounce Israel!’
units.rightText: And he took up his parable, and said, From Aram hath Balak brought me, The king of Moab from the mountains of the East: Come, curse me Jacob, And come, defy Israel.

units.leftText: How can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce those whom the LORD has not denounced?
units.rightText: How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? And how shall I defy, whom Jehovah hath not defied?

units.leftText: For I see them from atop the rocky cliffs, and I watch them from the hills. Behold, a people dwelling apart, not reckoning themselves among the nations.
units.rightText: For from the top of the rocks I see him, And from the hills I behold him: Lo, it is a people that dwelleth alone, And shall not be reckoned among the nations.

units.leftText: Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous; let my end be like theirs!”
units.rightText: Who can count the dust of Jacob, Or number the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, And let my last end be like his!

units.leftText: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and behold, you have only blessed them!”
units.rightText: And Balak said unto Balaam, What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them altogether.

units.leftText: But Balaam replied, “Should I not speak exactly what the LORD puts in my mouth?” Balaam’s Second Oracle
units.rightText: And he answered and said, Must I not take heed to speak that which Jehovah putteth in my mouth?

units.leftText: Then Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will only see the outskirts of their camp — not all of them. And from there, curse them for me.”
units.rightText: And Balak said unto him, Come, I pray thee, with me unto another place, from whence thou mayest see them; thou shalt see but the utmost part of them, and shalt not see them all: and curse me them from thence.

units.leftText: So Balak took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, where he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
units.rightText: And he took him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.

units.leftText: Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your burnt offering while I meet the LORD over there.”
units.rightText: And he said unto Balak, Stand here by thy burnt-offering, while I meet Jehovah yonder.

units.leftText: And the LORD met with Balaam and put a message in his mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and speak what I tell you.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah met Balaam, and put a word in his mouth, and said, Return unto Balak, and thus shalt thou speak.

units.leftText: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there by his burnt offering with the princes of Moab. “What did the LORD say?” Balak asked.
units.rightText: And he came to him, and, lo, he was standing by his burnt-offering, and the princes of Moab with him. And Balak said unto him, What hath Jehovah spoken?

units.leftText: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Arise, O Balak, and listen; give ear to me, O son of Zippor.
units.rightText: And he took up his parable, and said, Rise up, Balak, and hear; Hearken unto me, thou son of Zippor:

units.leftText: God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind. Does He speak and not act? Does He promise and not fulfill?
units.rightText: God is not a man, that he should lie, Neither the son of man, that he should repent: Hath he said, and will he not do it? Or hath he spoken, and will he not make it good?

units.leftText: I have indeed received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot change it.
units.rightText: Behold, I have received commandment to bless: And he hath blessed, and I cannot reverse it.

units.leftText: He considers no disaster for Jacob; He sees no trouble for Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of the King is among them.
units.rightText: He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob; Neither hath he seen perverseness in Israel: Jehovah his God is with him, And the shout of a king is among them.

units.leftText: God brought them out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox.
units.rightText: God bringeth them forth out of Egypt; He hath as it were the strength of the wild-ox.

units.leftText: For there is no spell against Jacob and no divination against Israel. It will now be said of Jacob and Israel, ‘What great things God has done!’
units.rightText: Surely there is no enchantment with Jacob; Neither is there any divination with Israel: Now shall it be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!

units.leftText: Behold, the people rise like a lioness; they rouse themselves like a lion, not resting until they devour their prey and drink the blood of the slain.”
units.rightText: Behold, the people riseth up as a lioness, And as a lion doth he lift himself up: He shall not lie down until he eat of the prey, And drink the blood of the slain.

units.leftText: Now Balak said to Balaam, “Then neither curse them at all nor bless them at all!”
units.rightText: And Balak said unto Balaam, Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all.

units.leftText: But Balaam replied, “Did I not tell you that whatever the LORD says, I must do?”
units.rightText: But Balaam answered and said unto Balak, Told not I thee, saying, All that Jehovah speaketh, that I must do?

units.leftText: “Please come,” said Balak, “I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God that you curse them for me from there.”
units.rightText: And Balak said unto Balaam, Come now, I will take thee unto another place; peradventure it will please God that thou mayest curse me them from thence.

units.leftText: And Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
units.rightText: And Balak took Balaam unto the top of Peor, that looketh down upon the desert.
leftNotes: 23:28 Or Jeshimon

units.leftText: Then Balaam said, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.

units.leftText: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
units.rightText: And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.

units.leftText: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not seek omens as on previous occasions, but he turned his face toward the wilderness.
units.rightText: And when Balaam saw that it pleased Jehovah to bless Israel, he went not, as at the other times, to meet with enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness.

units.leftText: When Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, the Spirit of God came upon him,
units.rightText: And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel dwelling according to their tribes; and the Spirit of God came upon him.

units.leftText: and he lifted up an oracle, saying: “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open,
