units.rightText: And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor saith, And the man whose eye was closed saith;

units.leftText: the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:
units.rightText: He saith, who heareth the words of God, Who seeth the vision of the Almighty, Falling down, and having his eyes open:
leftNotes: 24:4 Hebrew Shaddai; also in verse 16

units.leftText: How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
units.rightText: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, Thy tabernacles, O Israel!

units.leftText: They spread out like palm groves, like gardens beside a stream, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
units.rightText: As valleys are they spread forth, As gardens by the river-side, As lign-aloes which Jehovah hath planted, As cedar-trees beside the waters.
leftNotes: 24:6 Or like valleys

units.leftText: Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will have abundant water. His king will be greater than Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.
units.rightText: Water shall flow from his buckets, And his seed shall be in many waters, And his king shall be higher than Agag, And his kingdom shall be exalted.

units.leftText: God brought him out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox, to devour hostile nations and crush their bones, to pierce them with arrows.
units.rightText: God bringeth him forth out of Egypt; He hath as it were the strength of the wild-ox: He shall eat up the nations his adversaries, And shall break their bones in pieces, And smite them through with his arrows.

units.leftText: He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness— who dares to rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you and cursed are those who curse you.” Balak Dismisses Balaam
units.rightText: He couched, he lay down as a lion, And as a lioness; who shall rouse him up? Blessed be every one that blesseth thee, And cursed be every one that curseth thee.

units.leftText: Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together and said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have persisted in blessing them these three times.
units.rightText: And Balak’s anger was kindled against Balaam, and he smote his hands together; and Balak said unto Balaam, I called thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast altogether blessed them these three times.

units.leftText: Therefore , flee at once to your home! I said I would reward you richly, but instead the LORD has denied your reward.”
units.rightText: Therefore now flee thou to thy place: I thought to promote thee unto great honor; but, lo, Jehovah hath kept thee back from honor.

units.leftText: Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not already tell the messengers you sent me
units.rightText: And Balaam said unto Balak, Spake I not also to thy messengers that thou sentest unto me, saying,

units.leftText: that even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything of my own accord, good or bad, to go beyond the command of the LORD? I must speak whatever the LORD says.
units.rightText: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of Jehovah, to do either good or bad of mine own mind; what Jehovah speaketh, that will I speak?

units.leftText: Now I am going back to my people, but come, let me warn you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.” Balaam’s Fourth Oracle
units.rightText: And now, behold, I go unto my people: come, and I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.

units.leftText: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying, “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open,
units.rightText: And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor saith, And the man whose eye was closed saith;

units.leftText: the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:
units.rightText: He saith, who heareth the words of God, And knoweth the knowledge of the Most High, Who seeth the vision of the Almighty, Falling down, and having his eyes open:

units.leftText: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel. He will crush the skulls of Moab and strike down all the sons of Sheth.
units.rightText: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not nigh: There shall come forth a star out of Jacob, And a sceptre shall rise out of Israel, And shall smite through the corners of Moab, And break down all the sons of tumult.
leftNotes: 24:17 SP foreheads; Hebrew corners (of the head); LXX princes

units.leftText: Edom will become a possession, as will Seir, his enemy; but Israel will perform with valor.
units.rightText: And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession, who were his enemies; While Israel doeth valiantly.

units.leftText: A ruler will come from Jacob and destroy the survivors of the city.” Balaam’s Final Three Oracles
units.rightText: And out of Jacob shall one have dominion, And shall destroy the remnant from the city.

units.leftText: Then Balaam saw Amalek and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Amalek was first among the nations, but his end is destruction.”
units.rightText: And he looked on Amalek, and took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; But his latter end shall come to destruction.

units.leftText: Next he saw the Kenites and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in a cliff.
units.rightText: And he looked on the Kenite, and took up his parable, and said, Strong is thy dwelling-place, And thy nest is set in the rock.

units.leftText: Yet Kain will be destroyed when Asshur takes you captive.”
units.rightText: Nevertheless Kain shall be wasted, Until Asshur shall carry thee away captive.
leftNotes: 24:22 Or Assyria; also in verse 24

units.leftText: Once more Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?
units.rightText: And he took up his parable, and said, Alas, who shall live when God doeth this?

units.leftText: Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus; they will subdue Asshur and Eber, but they too will perish forever.”
units.rightText: But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim, And they shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber; And he also shall come to destruction.
leftNotes: 24:24 Hebrew Kittim

units.leftText: Then Balaam arose and returned to his homeland, and Balak also went on his way.
units.rightText: And Balaam rose up, and went and returned to his place; and Balak also went his way.

units.leftText: While Israel was staying in Shittim, the men began to indulge in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab,
units.rightText: And Israel abode in Shittim; and the people began to play the harlot with the daughters of Moab:
leftNotes: 25:1 Or Acacia Grove

units.leftText: who also invited them to the sacrifices for their gods. And the people ate and bowed down to these gods.
units.rightText: for they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods; and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.

units.leftText: So Israel joined in worshiping Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD burned against them.
units.rightText: And Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor: and the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and execute them in broad daylight before the LORD, so that His fierce anger may turn away from Israel.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Take all the chiefs of the people, and hang them up unto Jehovah before the sun, that the fierce anger of Jehovah may turn away from Israel.

units.leftText: So Moses told the judges of Israel, “Each of you must kill all of his men who have joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.” The Zeal of Phinehas
units.rightText: And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that have joined themselves unto Baal-peor.

units.leftText: Just then an Israelite man brought to his family a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation of Israel while they were weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, while they were weeping at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: On seeing this, Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, got up from the assembly, took a spear in his hand,
units.rightText: And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from the midst of the congregation, and took a spear in his hand;

units.leftText: followed the Israelite into the tent, and drove the spear through both of them— through the Israelite and on through the belly of the woman.
units.rightText: and he went after the man of Israel into the pavilion, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her body. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.

units.leftText: but those who died in the plague numbered 24,000.
units.rightText: And those that died by the plague were twenty and four thousand.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the Israelites; for he was zealous for My sake among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in My zeal.
units.rightText: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them, so that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy.

units.leftText: Declare, therefore, that I am granting him My covenant of peace.
units.rightText: Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace:

units.leftText: It will be a covenant of permanent priesthood for him and his descendants, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.”
units.rightText: and it shall be unto him, and to his seed after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was jealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel.

units.leftText: The name of the Israelite who was slain with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a Simeonite family.
units.rightText: Now the name of the man of Israel that was slain, who was slain with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a fathers’ house among the Simeonites.

units.leftText: And the name of the slain Midianite woman was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a Midianite family.
units.rightText: And the name of the Midianitish woman that was slain was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur; he was head of the people of a fathers’ house in Midian.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Attack the Midianites and strike them dead.
units.rightText: Vex the Midianites, and smite them;

units.leftText: For they assailed you deceitfully when they seduced you in the matter of Peor and their sister Cozbi, the daughter of the Midianite leader, the woman who was killed on the day the plague came because of Peor.”
units.rightText: for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of the prince of Midian, their sister, who was slain on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor.

units.leftText: After the plague had ended, the LORD said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,
units.rightText: And it came to pass after the plague, that Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, saying,

units.leftText: “Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by the houses of their fathers — all those twenty years of age or older who can serve in the army of Israel.”
units.rightText: Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by their fathers’ houses, all that are able to go forth to war in Israel.

units.leftText: So on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest issued the instruction,
units.rightText: And Moses and Eleazar the priest spake with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,

units.leftText: “Take a census of the men twenty years of age or older, as the LORD has commanded Moses.” And these were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt: The Tribe of Reuben
units.rightText: Take the sum of the people, from twenty years old and upward; as Jehovah commanded Moses and the children of Israel, that came forth out of the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 26:4 Take a census of the men is implied but not included in the Hebrew; see verse 2.

units.leftText: Reuben was the firstborn of Israel. These were the descendants of Reuben: The Hanochite clan from Hanoch, the Palluite clan from Pallu,
units.rightText: Reuben, the first-born of Israel; the sons of Reuben: of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites;

units.leftText: the Hezronite clan from Hezron, and the Carmite clan from Carmi.
units.rightText: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Reuben, and their registration numbered 43,730.
units.rightText: These are the families of the Reubenites; and they that were numbered of them were forty and three thousand and seven hundred and thirty.

units.leftText: Now the son of Pallu was Eliab,
units.rightText: And the sons of Pallu: Eliab.

units.leftText: and the sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram.
units.rightText: And the sons of Eliab: Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram. These are that Dathan and Abiram, who were called of the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against Jehovah,

units.leftText: And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, whose followers died when the fire consumed 250 men. They serve as a warning sign.
units.rightText: and the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company died; what time the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign.

units.leftText: However, the line of Korah did not die out. The Tribe of Simeon
units.rightText: Notwithstanding, the sons of Korah died not.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Simeon by their clans: The Nemuelite clan from Nemuel, the Jaminite clan from Jamin, the Jachinite clan from Jachin,
units.rightText: The sons of Simeon after their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites;
leftNotes: 26:12 Nemuel is another name for Jemuel; see Genesis 46:10|GEN 46:10*.

units.leftText: the Zerahite clan from Zerah, and the Shaulite clan from Shaul.
units.rightText: of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
leftNotes: 26:13 Zerah is a variant of Zohar; see Genesis 46:10|GEN 46:10* and Exodus 6:15.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Simeon, and there were 22,200 men. The Tribe of Gad
units.rightText: These are the families of the Simeonites, twenty and two thousand and two hundred.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Gad by their clans: The Zephonite clan from Zephon, the Haggite clan from Haggi, the Shunite clan from Shuni,
units.rightText: The sons of Gad after their families: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the family of the Haggites; of Shuni, the family of the Shunites;

units.leftText: the Oznite clan from Ozni, the Erite clan from Eri,
units.rightText: of Ozni, the family of the Oznites; of Eri, the family of the Erites;

units.leftText: the Arodite clan from Arod, and the Arelite clan from Areli.
units.rightText: of Arod, the family of the Arodites; of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
leftNotes: 26:17 SP and Syriac Arodi; see Genesis 46:16|GEN 46:16*.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Gad, and their registration numbered . . . 40,500. The Tribe of Judah
units.rightText: These are the families of the sons of Gad according to those that were numbered of them, forty thousand and five hundred.

units.leftText: The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, but they died in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: The sons of Judah: Er and Onan; and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Judah by their clans: The Shelanite clan from Shelah, the Perezite clan from Perez, and the Zerahite clan from Zerah.
units.rightText: And the sons of Judah after their families were: of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites; of Perez, the family of the Perezites; of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites.

units.leftText: And these were the descendants of Perez: the Hezronite clan from Hezron and the Hamulite clan from Hamul.
units.rightText: And the sons of Perez were: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Judah, and their registration numbered . . . 76,500. The Tribe of Issachar
units.rightText: These are the families of Judah according to those that were numbered of them, threescore and sixteen thousand and five hundred.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Issachar by their clans: The Tolaite clan from Tola, the Punite clan from Puvah,
units.rightText: The sons of Issachar after their families: of Tola, the family of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the family of the Punites;
leftNotes: 26:23 SP, LXX, Vulgate, and Syriac the Puite clan from Puah; see 1 Chronicles 7:1|1CH 7:1*.

units.leftText: the Jashubite clan from Jashub, and the Shimronite clan from Shimron.
units.rightText: of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
leftNotes: 26:24 Jashub is a variant of Job; see Genesis 46:13|GEN 46:13*.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Issachar, and their registration numbered . . . 64,300. The Tribe of Zebulun
units.rightText: These are the families of Issachar according to those that were numbered of them, threescore and four thousand and three hundred.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Zebulun by their clans: The Seredite clan from Sered, the Elonite clan from Elon, and the Jahleelite clan from Jahleel.
units.rightText: The sons of Zebulun after their families: of Sered, the family of the Seredites; of Elon, the family of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Zebulun, and their registration numbered . . . 60,500. The Tribe of Manasseh
units.rightText: These are the families of the Zebulunites according to those that were numbered of them, threescore thousand and five hundred.

units.leftText: The descendants of Joseph included the clans of Manasseh and Ephraim.
units.rightText: The sons of Joseph after their families: Manasseh and Ephraim.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Manasseh: The Machirite clan from Machir, the father of Gilead, and the Gileadite clan from Gilead.
units.rightText: The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the family of the Machirites; and Machir begat Gilead: of Gilead, the family of the Gileadites.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Gilead: the Iezerite clan from Iezer, the Helekite clan from Helek,
units.rightText: These are the sons of Gilead: of Iezer, the family of the Iezerites; of Helek, the family of the Helekites;
leftNotes: 26:30 Iezer is a variant of Abiezer; see Joshua 17:2|JOS 17:2*.

units.leftText: the Asrielite clan from Asriel, the Shechemite clan from Shechem,
units.rightText: and of Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; and of Shechem, the family of the Shechemites;

units.leftText: the Shemidaite clan from Shemida, and the Hepherite clan from Hepher.
units.rightText: and of Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; and of Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.

units.leftText: Now Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons but only daughters. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
units.rightText: And Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Manasseh, and their registration numbered . . . 52,700. The Tribe of Ephraim
units.rightText: These are the families of Manasseh; and they that were numbered of them were fifty and two thousand and seven hundred.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: The Shuthelahite clan from Shuthelah, the Becherite clan from Becher, and the Tahanite clan from Tahan.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Ephraim after their families: of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the family of the Becherites; of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.

units.leftText: And the descendants of Shuthelah were the Eranite clan from Eran.
units.rightText: And these are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the family of the Eranites.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Ephraim, and their registration numbered . . . 32,500. These clans were the descendants of Joseph. The Tribe of Benjamin
units.rightText: These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to those that were numbered of them, thirty and two thousand and five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph after their families.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans: The Belaite clan from Bela, the Ashbelite clan from Ashbel, the Ahiramite clan from Ahiram,
units.rightText: The sons of Benjamin after their families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites;

units.leftText: the Shuphamite clan from Shupham, and the Huphamite clan from Hupham.
units.rightText: of Shephupham, the family of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
leftNotes: 26:39 A few MT manuscripts, SP, Vulgate, and Syriac (see also LXX); most MT manuscripts Shephupham

units.leftText: And the descendants of Bela from Ard and Naaman were the Ardite clan from Ard and the Naamite clan from Naaman.
units.rightText: And the sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: of Ard, the family of the Ardites; of Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
leftNotes: 26:40 SP and Vulgate (see also LXX); MT does not include from Ard.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Benjamin, and their registration numbered . . . 45,600. The Tribe of Dan
units.rightText: These are the sons of Benjamin after their families; and they that were numbered of them were forty and five thousand and six hundred.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: The Shuhamite clan from Shuham.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Dan after their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan after their families.

units.leftText: All of them were Shuhamite clans, and their registration numbered . . . 64,400. The Tribe of Asher
units.rightText: All the families of the Shuhamites, according to those that were numbered of them, were threescore and four thousand and four hundred.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Asher by their clans: The Imnite clan from Imnah, the Ishvite clan from Ishvi, and the Beriite clan from Beriah.
units.rightText: The sons of Asher after their families: of Imnah, the family of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the family of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the family of the Berites.

units.leftText: And these were the descendants of Beriah: the Heberite clan from Heber and the Malchielite clan from Malchiel.
units.rightText: Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites.

units.leftText: And the name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
units.rightText: And the name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Asher, and their registration numbered . . . 53,400. The Tribe of Naphtali
units.rightText: These are the families of the sons of Asher according to those that were numbered of them, fifty and three thousand and four hundred.

units.leftText: These were the descendants of Naphtali by their clans: The Jahzeelite clan from Jahzeel, the Gunite clan from Guni,
units.rightText: The sons of Naphtali after their families: of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the family of the Gunites;

units.leftText: the Jezerite clan from Jezer, and the Shillemite clan from Shillem.
units.rightText: of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.

units.leftText: These were the clans of Naphtali, and their registration numbered . . . 45,400.
units.rightText: These are the families of Naphtali according to their families; and they that were numbered of them were forty and five thousand and four hundred.

units.leftText: These men of Israel numbered 601,730 in all. Inheritance by Lot
units.rightText: These are they that were numbered of the children of Israel, six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “The land is to be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, according to the number of names.
units.rightText: Unto these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names.

units.leftText: Increase the inheritance for a large tribe and decrease it for a small one; each tribe is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those registered.
units.rightText: To the more thou shalt give the more inheritance, and to the fewer thou shalt give the less inheritance: to every one according to those that were numbered of him shall his inheritance be given.

units.leftText: Indeed, the land must be divided by lot; they shall receive their inheritance according to the names of the tribes of their fathers.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding, the land shall be divided by lot: according to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.

units.leftText: Each inheritance is to be divided by lot among the larger and smaller tribes.” The Levites Numbered
units.rightText: According to the lot shall their inheritance be divided between the more and the fewer.

units.leftText: Now these were the Levites numbered by their clans: The Gershonite clan from Gershon, the Kohathite clan from Kohath, and the Merarite clan from Merari.
units.rightText: And these are they that were numbered of the Levites after their families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites; of Merari, the family of the Merarites.

units.leftText: These were the families of the Levites: The Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, and the Korahite clan.
units.rightText: These are the families of Levi: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, the family of the Korahites. And Kohath begat Amram.

units.leftText: and Amram’s wife was named Jochebed. She was also a daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. To Amram she bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.
units.rightText: And the name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt: and she bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.

units.leftText: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were born to Aaron,
units.rightText: And unto Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

units.leftText: but Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Nadab and Abihu died, when they offered strange fire before Jehovah.
leftNotes: 26:61 Or strange

units.leftText: The registration of the Levites totaled 23,000, every male a month old or more; they were not numbered among the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites. Only Caleb and Joshua Remain
units.rightText: And they that were numbered of them were twenty and three thousand, every male from a month old and upward: for they were not numbered among the children of Israel, because there was no inheritance given them among the children of Israel.

units.leftText: These were the ones numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest when they counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
units.rightText: These are they that were numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who numbered the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.

units.leftText: Among all these, however, there was not one who had been numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai.
units.rightText: But among these there was not a man of them that were numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest, who numbered the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.

units.leftText: For the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness. Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
units.rightText: For Jehovah had said of them, They shall surely die in the wilderness. And there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.

units.leftText: Now the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They approached
units.rightText: Then drew near the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph; and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.

units.leftText: the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation, and said,
units.rightText: And they stood before Moses, and before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, at the door of the tent of meeting, saying,

units.leftText: “Our father died in the wilderness, but he was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD. Instead, he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
units.rightText: Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not among the company of them that gathered themselves together against Jehovah in the company of Korah: but he died in his own sin; and he had no sons.

units.leftText: Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan because he had no sons? Give us property among our father’s brothers.”
units.rightText: Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give unto us a possession among the brethren of our father.

units.leftText: So Moses brought their case before the LORD,
units.rightText: And Moses brought their cause before Jehovah.

units.leftText: and the LORD answered him,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly. You certainly must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers and transfer their father’s inheritance to them.
units.rightText: The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.

units.leftText: Furthermore, you shall say to the Israelites, ‘If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
units.rightText: And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter.

units.leftText: If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.
units.rightText: And if he have no daughter, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his brethren.

units.leftText: If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.
units.rightText: And if he have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his father’s brethren.

units.leftText: And if his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to the next of kin from his clan, that he may take possession of it. This is to be a statutory ordinance for the Israelites, as the LORD has commanded Moses.’” Moses Requests a Successor (Deuteronomy 3:23–29|DEU 3:23-29*)
units.rightText: And if his father have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his kinsman that is next to him of his family, and he shall possess it: and it shall be unto the children of Israel a statute and ordinance, as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Get thee up into this mountain of Abarim, and behold the land which I have given unto the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 27:12 LXX Go up Mount Nebo beyond the Jordan

units.leftText: After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was;
units.rightText: And when thou hast seen it, thou also shalt be gathered unto thy people, as Aaron thy brother was gathered;

units.leftText: for when the congregation contended in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters.” Those were the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin.
units.rightText: because ye rebelled against my word in the wilderness of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to sanctify me at the waters before their eyes. (These are the waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)
leftNotes: 27:14 Meribah means quarreling; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*.

units.leftText: So Moses appealed to the LORD,
units.rightText: And Moses spake unto Jehovah, saying,

units.leftText: “May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation
units.rightText: Let Jehovah, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,

units.leftText: who will go out and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd.” Joshua to Succeed Moses (Deuteronomy 31:1–8|DEU 31:1-8*)
units.rightText: who may go out before them, and who may come in before them, and who may lead them out, and who may bring them in; that the congregation of Jehovah be not as sheep which have no shepherd.

units.leftText: And the LORD replied to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay thy hand upon him;

units.leftText: Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.
units.rightText: and set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and give him a charge in their sight.

units.leftText: Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him.
units.rightText: And thou shalt put of thine honor upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may obey.

units.leftText: He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim. At his command, he and all the Israelites with him— the entire congregation— will go out and come in.”
units.rightText: And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before Jehovah: at his word shall they go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation.
leftNotes: 27:21 Literally the Lights

units.leftText: Moses did as the LORD had commanded him. He took Joshua, had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation,
units.rightText: And Moses did as Jehovah commanded him; and he took Joshua, and set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation:

units.leftText: and laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had instructed through Moses.
units.rightText: and he laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as Jehovah spake by Moses.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Command the Israelites and say to them: See that you present to Me at its appointed time the food for My food offerings, as a pleasing aroma to Me.
units.rightText: Command the children of Israel, and say unto them, My oblation, my food for my offerings made by fire, of a sweet savor unto me, shall ye observe to offer unto me in their due season.

units.leftText: And tell them that this is the food offering you are to present to the LORD as a regular burnt offering each day: two unblemished year-old male lambs.
units.rightText: And thou shalt say unto them, This is the offering made by fire which ye shall offer unto Jehovah: he-lambs a year old without blemish, two day by day, for a continual burnt-offering.

units.leftText: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
units.rightText: The one lamb shalt thou offer in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou offer at even;
leftNotes: 28:4 Hebrew between the two evenings; also in verse 8

units.leftText: along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives.
units.rightText: and the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil.
leftNotes: 28:5 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour); also in verses 13, 21, and 29.
28:5 Or a quarter hin of pure olive oil; Hebrew a quarter hin of pressed oil; that is, approximately 0.97 quarts or 0.92 liters; similarly in verses 7 and 14

units.leftText: This is a regular burnt offering established at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: It is a continual burnt-offering, which was ordained in mount Sinai for a sweet savor, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: The drink offering accompanying each lamb shall be a quarter hin. Pour out the offering of fermented drink to the LORD in the sanctuary area.
units.rightText: And the drink-offering thereof shall be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb: in the holy place shalt thou pour out a drink-offering of strong drink unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: And offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. The Sabbath Offerings
units.rightText: And the other lamb shalt thou offer at even: as the meal-offering of the morning, and as the drink-offering thereof, thou shalt offer it, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: On the Sabbath day, present two unblemished year-old male lambs, accompanied by a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, as well as a drink offering.
units.rightText: And on the sabbath day two he-lambs a year old without blemish, and two tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, and the drink-offering thereof:
leftNotes: 28:9 Two-tenths of an ephah is approximately 4 dry quarts or 4.4 liters (probably about 5.1 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of flour); also in verses 12, 20, and 28.

units.leftText: This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering. The Monthly Offerings
units.rightText: this is the burnt-offering of every sabbath, besides the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: At the beginning of every month, you are to present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt-offering unto Jehovah: two young bullocks, and one ram, seven he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with the ram,
units.rightText: and three tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, for each bullock; and two tenth parts of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, for the one ram;
leftNotes: 28:12 Three-tenths of an ephah is approximately 6 dry quarts or 6.6 liters (probably about 7.6 pounds or 3.5 kilograms of flour); also in verses 20 and 28.

units.leftText: and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each lamb. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: and a tenth part of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering unto every lamb; for a burnt-offering of a sweet savor, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine with each bull, a third of a hin with the ram, and a quarter hin with each lamb. This is the monthly burnt offering to be made at each new moon throughout the year.
units.rightText: And their drink-offerings shall be half a hin of wine for a bullock, and the third part of a hin for the ram, and the fourth part of a hin for a lamb: this is the burnt-offering of every month throughout the months of the year.
leftNotes: 28:14 Half a hin is approximately 1.9 quarts or 1.8 liters of wine.
28:14 A third of a hin is approximately 1.3 quarts or 1.2 liters of wine.

units.leftText: In addition to the regular burnt offering with its drink offering, one male goat is to be presented to the LORD as a sin offering. Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread (Exodus 12:14–28|EXO 12:14-28*; Leviticus 23:4–8|LEV 23:4-8*; Deuteronomy 16:1–8|DEU 16:1-8*)
units.rightText: And one he-goat for a sin-offering unto Jehovah; it shall be offered besides the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: The fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD’s Passover.
units.rightText: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is Jehovah’s passover.

units.leftText: On the fifteenth day of this month, there shall be a feast; for seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.
units.rightText: And on the fifteenth day of this month shall be a feast: seven days shall unleavened bread be eaten.

units.leftText: On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.
units.rightText: In the first day shall be a holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work;

units.leftText: Present to the LORD a food offering, a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
units.rightText: but ye shall offer an offering made by fire, a burnt-offering unto Jehovah: two young bullocks, and one ram, and seven he-lambs a year old; they shall be unto you without blemish;

units.leftText: The grain offering shall consist of fine flour mixed with oil; offer three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
units.rightText: and their meal-offering, fine flour mingled with oil: three tenth parts shall ye offer for a bullock, and two tenth parts for the ram;

units.leftText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.
units.rightText: a tenth part shalt thou offer for every lamb of the seven lambs;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering, to make atonement for you.

units.leftText: You are to present these in addition to the regular morning burnt offering.
units.rightText: Ye shall offer these besides the burnt-offering of the morning, which is for a continual burnt-offering.

units.leftText: Offer the same food each day for seven days as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It is to be offered with its drink offering and the regular burnt offering.
units.rightText: After this manner ye shall offer daily, for seven days, the food of the offering made by fire, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah: it shall be offered besides the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: On the seventh day you shall hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work. The Feast of Weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9–12|DEU 16:9-12*)
units.rightText: And on the seventh day ye shall have a holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work.

units.leftText: On the day of firstfruits, when you present an offering of new grain to the LORD during the Feast of Weeks, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.
units.rightText: Also in the day of the first-fruits, when ye offer a new meal-offering unto Jehovah in your feast of weeks, ye shall have a holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work;
leftNotes: 28:26 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Pentecost(see Acts 2:1|ACT 2:1*).

units.leftText: Present a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old as a pleasing aroma to the LORD,
units.rightText: but ye shall offer a burnt-offering for a sweet savor unto Jehovah: two young bullocks, one ram, seven he-lambs a year old;

units.leftText: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
units.rightText: and their meal-offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts for each bullock, two tenth parts for the one ram,

units.leftText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.
units.rightText: a tenth part for every lamb of the seven lambs;

units.leftText: Include one male goat to make atonement for you.
units.rightText: one he-goat, to make atonement for you.

units.leftText: Offer them with their drink offerings in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. The animals must be unblemished.[’’]
units.rightText: Besides the continual burnt-offering, and the meal-offering thereof, ye shall offer them (they shall be unto you without blemish), and their drink-offerings.

units.leftText: “On the first day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you must not do any regular work. This will be a day for you to sound the trumpets.
units.rightText: And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, ye shall have a holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work: it is a day of blowing of trumpets unto you.

units.leftText: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And ye shall offer a burnt-offering for a sweet savor unto Jehovah: one young bullock, one ram, seven he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
units.rightText: and their meal-offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts for the bullock, two tenth parts for the ram,
leftNotes: 29:3 Three-tenths of an ephah is approximately 6 dry quarts or 6.6 liters (probably about 7.6 pounds or 3.5 kilograms of flour); also in verses 9 and 14.
29:3 Two-tenths of an ephah is approximately 4 dry quarts or 4.4 liters (probably about 5.1 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of flour); also in verses 9 and 14.

units.leftText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven male lambs.
units.rightText: and one tenth part for every lamb of the seven lambs;
leftNotes: 29:4 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour); also in verses 10 and 15.

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering, to make atonement for you;

units.leftText: These are in addition to the monthly and daily burnt offerings with their prescribed grain offerings and drink offerings. They are a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD. The Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:1–34|LEV 16:1-34*; Leviticus 23:26–32|LEV 23:26-32*)
units.rightText: besides the burnt-offering of the new moon, and the meal-offering thereof, and the continual burnt-offering and the meal-offering thereof, and their drink-offerings, according unto their ordinance, for a sweet savor, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: On the tenth day of this seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you shall humble yourselves; you must not do any work.
units.rightText: And on the tenth day of this seventh month ye shall have a holy convocation; and ye shall afflict your souls: ye shall do no manner of work;
leftNotes: 29:7 Or afflict your souls or deny yourselves

units.leftText: Present as a pleasing aroma to the LORD a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: but ye shall offer a burnt-offering unto Jehovah for a sweet savor: one young bullock, one ram, seven he-lambs a year old; they shall be unto you without blemish;

units.leftText: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
units.rightText: and their meal-offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts for the bullock, two tenth parts for the one ram,

units.leftText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.
units.rightText: a tenth part for every lamb of the seven lambs:

units.leftText: Include one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings. The Feast of Tabernacles (Deuteronomy 16:13–17|DEU 16:13-17*)
units.rightText: one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the sin-offering of atonement, and the continual burnt-offering, and the meal-offering thereof, and their drink-offerings.

units.leftText: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work, and you shall observe a feast to the LORD for seven days.
units.rightText: And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month ye shall have a holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work, and ye shall keep a feast unto Jehovah seven days:

units.leftText: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a food offering, a burnt offering of thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: and ye shall offer a burnt-offering, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah; thirteen young bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old; they shall be without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil with each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths of an ephah with each of the two rams,
units.rightText: and their meal-offering, fine flour mingled with oil, three tenth parts for every bullock of the thirteen bullocks, two tenth parts for each ram of the two rams,

units.leftText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the fourteen lambs.
units.rightText: and a tenth part for every lamb of the fourteen lambs;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: On the second day you are to present twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And on the second day ye shall offer twelve young bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
units.rightText: and their meal-offering and their drink-offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, and the meal-offering thereof, and their drink-offerings.

units.leftText: On the third day you are to present eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And on the third day eleven bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
units.rightText: and their meal-offering and their drink-offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, and the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: On the fourth day you are to present ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And on the fourth day ten bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
units.rightText: their meal-offering and their drink-offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: On the fifth day you are to present nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And on the fifth day nine bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
units.rightText: and their meal-offering and their drink-offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, and the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: On the sixth day you are to present eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And on the sixth day eight bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
units.rightText: and their meal-offering and their drink-offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offerings thereof.

units.leftText: On the seventh day you are to present seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: And on the seventh day seven bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
units.rightText: and their meal-offering and their drink-offerings for the bullocks, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: On the eighth day you are to hold a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work.
units.rightText: On the eighth day ye shall have a solemn assembly: ye shall do no servile work;

units.leftText: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a food offering, a burnt offering of one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
units.rightText: but ye shall offer a burnt-offering, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor unto Jehovah: one bullock, one ram, seven he-lambs a year old without blemish;

units.leftText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
units.rightText: their meal-offering and their drink-offerings for the bullock, for the ram, and for the lambs, shall be according to their number, after the ordinance:

units.leftText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
units.rightText: and one he-goat for a sin-offering; besides the continual burnt-offering, and the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.

units.leftText: You are to present these offerings to the LORD at your appointed times, in addition to your vow and freewill offerings, whether burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings.”
units.rightText: These ye shall offer unto Jehovah in your set feasts, besides your vows, and your freewill-offerings, for your burnt-offerings, and for your meal-offerings, and for your drink-offerings, and for your peace-offerings.

units.leftText: So Moses spoke all this to the Israelites just as the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And Moses told the children of Israel according to all that Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Then Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
units.rightText: And Moses spake unto the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which Jehovah hath commanded.

units.leftText: If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised.
units.rightText: When a man voweth a vow unto Jehovah, or sweareth an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.
leftNotes: 30:2 Cited in Matthew 5:33|MAT 5:33*

units.leftText: And if a woman in her father’s house during her youth makes a vow to the LORD or obligates herself by a pledge,
units.rightText: Also when a woman voweth a vow unto Jehovah, and bindeth herself by a bond, being in her father’s house, in her youth,

units.leftText: and her father hears about her vow or pledge but says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
units.rightText: and her father heareth her vow, and her bond wherewith she hath bound her soul, and her father holdeth his peace at her; then all her vows shall stand, and every bond wherewith she hath bound her soul shall stand.

units.leftText: But if her father prohibits her on the day he hears about it, then none of the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her.
units.rightText: But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth, none of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and Jehovah will forgive her, because her father disallowed her.

units.leftText: If a woman marries while under a vow or rash promise by which she has bound herself,
units.rightText: And if she be married to a husband, while her vows are upon her, or the rash utterance of her lips, wherewith she hath bound her soul,

units.leftText: and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her on that day, then the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
units.rightText: and her husband hear it, and hold his peace at her in the day that he heareth it; then her vows shall stand, and her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul shall stand.

units.leftText: But if her husband prohibits her when he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her or the rash promise she has made, and the LORD will absolve her.
units.rightText: But if her husband disallow her in the day that he heareth it, then he shall make void her vow which is upon her, and the rash utterance of her lips, wherewith she hath bound her soul: and Jehovah will forgive her.

units.leftText: Every vow a widow or divorced woman pledges to fulfill is binding on her.
units.rightText: But the vow of a widow, or of her that is divorced, even everything wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand against her.

units.leftText: If a woman in her husband’s house has made a vow or put herself under an obligation with an oath,
units.rightText: And if she vowed in her husband’s house, or bound her soul by a bond with an oath,

units.leftText: and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her and does not prohibit her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
units.rightText: and her husband heard it, and held his peace at her, and disallowed her not; then all her vows shall stand, and every bond wherewith she bound her soul shall stand.

units.leftText: But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether her vows or pledges, shall stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will absolve her.
units.rightText: But if her husband made them null and void in the day that he heard them, then whatsoever proceeded out of her lips concerning her vows, or concerning the bond of her soul, shall not stand: her husband hath made them void; and Jehovah will forgive her.

units.leftText: Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow or any sworn pledge to deny herself.
units.rightText: Every vow, and every binding oath to afflict the soul, her husband may establish it, or her husband may make it void.
leftNotes: 30:13 Or to fast

units.leftText: But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all the vows and pledges that bind her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard about them.
units.rightText: But if her husband altogether hold his peace at her from day to day, then he establisheth all her vows, or all her bonds, which are upon her: he hath established them, because he held his peace at her in the day that he heard them.

units.leftText: But if he nullifies them after he hears of them, then he will bear her iniquity.”
units.rightText: But if he shall make them null and void after that he hath heard them, then he shall bear her iniquity.

units.leftText: These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the relationship between a man and his wife, and between a father and a young daughter still in his home.
units.rightText: These are the statutes, which Jehovah commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter, being in her youth, in her father’s house.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites. After that, you will be gathered to your people.”
units.rightText: Avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites: afterward shalt thou be gathered unto thy people.

units.leftText: So Moses told the people, “Arm some of your men for war, that they may go against the Midianites and execute the LORD’s vengeance on them.
units.rightText: And Moses spake unto the people, saying, Arm ye men from among you for the war, that they may go against Midian, to execute Jehovah’s vengeance on Midian.

units.leftText: Send into battle a thousand men from each tribe of Israel.”
units.rightText: Of every tribe a thousand, throughout all the tribes of Israel, shall ye send to the war.

units.leftText: So a thousand men were recruited from each tribe of Israel— twelve thousand armed for war.
units.rightText: So there were delivered, out of the thousands of Israel, a thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.

units.leftText: And Moses sent the thousand from each tribe into battle, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took with him the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for signaling.
units.rightText: And Moses sent them, a thousand of every tribe, to the war, them and Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, to the war, with the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for the alarm in his hand.

units.leftText: Then they waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
units.rightText: And they warred against Midian, as Jehovah commanded Moses; and they slew every male.

units.leftText: Among the slain were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba— the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
units.rightText: And they slew the kings of Midian with the rest of their slain: Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.

units.leftText: The Israelites captured the Midianite women and their children, and they plundered all their herds, flocks, and goods.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel took captive the women of Midian and their little ones; and all their cattle, and all their flocks, and all their goods, they took for a prey.

units.leftText: Then they burned all the cities where the Midianites had lived, as well as all their encampments,
units.rightText: And all their cities in the places wherein they dwelt, and all their encampments, they burnt with fire.

units.leftText: and carried away all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals.
units.rightText: And they took all the spoil, and all the prey, both of man and of beast.

units.leftText: They brought the captives, spoils, and plunder to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of Israel at the camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
units.rightText: And they brought the captives, and the prey, and the spoil, unto Moses, and unto Eleazar the priest, and unto the congregation of the children of Israel, unto the camp at the plains of Moab, which are by the Jordan at Jericho.

units.leftText: And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went to meet them outside the camp.
units.rightText: And Moses, and Eleazar the priest, and all the princes of the congregation, went forth to meet them without the camp.

units.leftText: But Moses was angry with the officers of the army — the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds — who were returning from the battle.
units.rightText: And Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, who came from the service of the war.

units.leftText: “Have you spared all the women?” he asked them.
units.rightText: And Moses said unto them, Have ye saved all the women alive?

units.leftText: “Look, these women caused the sons of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to turn unfaithfully against the LORD at Peor, so that the plague struck the congregation of the LORD.
units.rightText: Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Jehovah in the matter of Peor, and so the plague was among the congregation of Jehovah.

units.leftText: So now, kill all the boys, as well as every woman who has had relations with a man,
units.rightText: Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman that hath known man by lying with him.

units.leftText: but spare for yourselves every girl who has never had relations with a man.
units.rightText: But all the women-children, that have not known man by lying with him, keep alive for yourselves.

units.leftText: All of you who have killed a person or touched the dead are to remain outside the camp for seven days. On the third day and the seventh day you are to purify both yourselves and your captives.
units.rightText: And encamp ye without the camp seven days: whosoever hath killed any person, and whosoever hath touched any slain, purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, ye and your captives.

units.leftText: And purify every garment and leather good, everything made of goat’s hair, and every article of wood.”
units.rightText: And as to every garment, and all that is made of skin, and all work of goats’ hair, and all things made of wood, ye shall purify yourselves.

units.leftText: Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, “This is the statute of the law which the LORD has commanded Moses:
units.rightText: And Eleazar the priest said unto the men of war that went to the battle, This is the statute of the law which Jehovah hath commanded Moses:

units.leftText: Only the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—
units.rightText: howbeit the gold, and the silver, the brass, the iron, the tin, and the lead,

units.leftText: everything that can withstand the fire— must be put through the fire, and it will be clean. But it must still be purified with the water of purification. And everything that cannot withstand the fire must pass through the water.
units.rightText: everything that may abide the fire, ye shall make to go through the fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it shall be purified with the water for impurity: and all that abideth not the fire ye shall make to go through the water.

units.leftText: On the seventh day you are to wash your clothes, and you will be clean. After that you may enter the camp.” Division of the Spoils
units.rightText: And ye shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and ye shall be clean; and afterward ye shall come into the camp.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “You and Eleazar the priest and the family heads of the congregation are to take a count of what was captured, both of man and beast.
units.rightText: Take the sum of the prey that was taken, both of man and of beast, thou, and Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the congregation;

units.leftText: Then divide the captives between the troops who went out to battle and the rest of the congregation.
units.rightText: and divide the prey into two parts: between the men skilled in war, that went out to battle, and all the congregation.

units.leftText: Set aside a tribute for the LORD from what belongs to the soldiers who went into battle: one out of every five hundred, whether persons, cattle, donkeys, or sheep.
units.rightText: And levy a tribute unto Jehovah of the men of war that went out to battle: one soul of five hundred, both of the persons, and of the oxen, and of the asses, and of the flocks:

units.leftText: Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: take it of their half, and give it unto Eleazar the priest, for Jehovah’s heave-offering.

units.leftText: From the Israelites’ half, take one out of every fifty, whether persons, cattle, donkeys, sheep, or other animals, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD.”
units.rightText: And of the children of Israel’s half, thou shalt take one drawn out of every fifty, of the persons, of the oxen, of the asses, and of the flocks, even of all the cattle, and give them unto the Levites, that keep the charge of the tabernacle of Jehovah.

units.leftText: So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses,
units.rightText: And Moses and Eleazar the priest did as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: and this plunder remained from the spoils the soldiers had taken: 675,000 sheep,
units.rightText: Now the prey, over and above the booty which the men of war took, was six hundred thousand and seventy thousand and five thousand sheep,

units.leftText: 72,000 cattle,
units.rightText: and threescore and twelve thousand oxen,

units.leftText: 61,000 donkeys,
units.rightText: and threescore and one thousand asses,

units.leftText: and 32,000 women who had not slept with a man.
units.rightText: and thirty and two thousand persons in all, of the women that had not known man by lying with him.

units.leftText: This was the half portion for those who had gone to war:
units.rightText: And the half, which was the portion of them that went out to war, was in number three hundred thousand and thirty thousand and seven thousand and five hundred sheep:

units.leftText: including a tribute to the LORD of 675,
units.rightText: and Jehovah’s tribute of the sheep was six hundred and threescore and fifteen.

units.leftText: 36,000 cattle, including a tribute to the LORD of 72,
units.rightText: And the oxen were thirty and six thousand; of which Jehovah’s tribute was threescore and twelve.

units.leftText: 30,500 donkeys, including a tribute to the LORD of 61,
units.rightText: And the asses were thirty thousand and five hundred; of which Jehovah’s tribute was threescore and one.

units.leftText: and 16,000 people, including a tribute to the LORD of 32.
units.rightText: And the persons were sixteen thousand; of whom Jehovah’s tribute was thirty and two persons.

units.leftText: Moses gave the tribute to Eleazar the priest as an offering for the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And Moses gave the tribute, which was Jehovah’s heave-offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: From the Israelites’ half, which Moses had set apart from the men who had gone to war,
units.rightText: And of the children of Israel’s half, which Moses divided off from the men that warred

units.leftText: this half belonged to the congregation: 337,500 sheep,
units.rightText: (now the congregation’s half was three hundred thousand and thirty thousand, seven thousand and five hundred sheep,

units.leftText: 36,000 cattle,
units.rightText: and thirty and six thousand oxen,

units.leftText: 30,500 donkeys,
units.rightText: and thirty thousand and five hundred asses,

units.leftText: and 16,000 people.
units.rightText: and sixteen thousand persons),

units.leftText: From the Israelites’ half, Moses took one out of every fifty persons and animals and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded him. The Voluntary Offering
units.rightText: even of the children of Israel’s half, Moses took one drawn out of every fifty, both of man and of beast, and gave them unto the Levites, that kept the charge of the tabernacle of Jehovah; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Then the officers who were over the units of the army — the commanders of thousands and of hundreds — approached Moses
units.rightText: And the officers that were over the thousands of the host, the captains of thousands, and the captains of hundreds, came near unto Moses;

units.leftText: and said, “Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one of us is missing.
units.rightText: and they said unto Moses, Thy servants have taken the sum of the men of war that are under our charge, and there lacketh not one man of us.

units.leftText: So we have brought to the LORD an offering of the gold articles each man acquired— armlets, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces— to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD.”
units.rightText: And we have brought Jehovah’s oblation, what every man hath gotten, of jewels of gold, ankle-chains, and bracelets, signet-rings, ear-rings, and armlets, to make atonement for our souls before Jehovah.

units.leftText: So Moses and Eleazar the priest received from them all the articles made out of gold.
units.rightText: And Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of them, even all wrought jewels.

units.leftText: All the gold that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds presented as an offering to the LORD weighed 16,750 shekels.
units.rightText: And all the gold of the heave-offering that they offered up to Jehovah, of the captains of thousands, and of the captains of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.
leftNotes: 31:52 16,750 shekels is approximately 420.8 pounds or 190.9 kilograms.

units.leftText: Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.
units.rightText: ( For the men of war had taken booty, every man for himself.)

units.leftText: And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the tent of meeting, for a memorial for the children of Israel before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now the Reubenites and Gadites, who had very large herds and flocks, surveyed the lands of Jazer and Gilead, and they saw that the region was suitable for livestock.
units.rightText: Now the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle: and when they saw the land of Jazer, and the land of Gilead, that, behold, the place was a place for cattle;

units.leftText: So the Gadites and Reubenites came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, and said,
units.rightText: the children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spake unto Moses, and to Eleazar the priest, and unto the princes of the congregation, saying,

units.leftText: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
units.rightText: Ataroth, and Dibon, and Jazer, and Nimrah, and Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Sebam, and Nebo, and Beon,
leftNotes: 32:3 Hebrew; see verse 38, and similarly in SP and LXX Sibmah

units.leftText: which the LORD conquered before the congregation of Israel, are suitable for livestock — and your servants have livestock.”
units.rightText: the land which Jehovah smote before the congregation of Israel, is a land for cattle; and thy servants have cattle.
